She added, “But my favorite woman in film is my mom, Leslie Mann.” Francesca Amiker, Tessa Thompson, Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig, wearing Max Mara, speak onstage at the 2025 WIF Honors Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Janicza Bravo presented the the Crystal Award for Advocacy in Film award to Hedda ’s Tessa Thompson, Nia DaCosta (not present), Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig. Lastly, Kaia Gerber honored her Palm Royale co-star Kristen Wiig with the inaugural Icon Award. “Who better to receive it than my favorite scene partner?” Gerber said. “For seven years at SNL , Kristen showed us comedy could be completely unhinged and utterly ‘stupid’ — a word I learned from Kristen herself as one of the highest forms of praise in comedy — and also, somehow be simultaneously deeply human.” Kaia Gerber, Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF and Icon Award recipient Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Gerber continued, “When Bridesmaids came out, it was a revelation. … There is such truth and utter heartbreak behind [all of her characters].” She finished, “Tonight, we celebrate the woman who taught us that comedy is art, that chaos is beautiful, that sheer stupidity is not only encouraged but a necessity of life and that being unapologetically yourself might just be the most iconic move of all.” An emotional Wiig thanked Gerber, who she called “a lighthouse” on her show. “I’m fully overwhelmed,” she said. “This is my first time having to make a speech like this. I just kept thinking, ‘How did I get here?’ … I keep coming back to the people who said ‘yes’ to me before I had anything on my resume.” Wiig noted how her whole life changed when she joined The Groundlings. “That led to SNL ,” she said. She called out two men: Bridesmaids director Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow (who reached out to her and asked if she wanted to write something). “I certainly wouldn’t be up here getting an award from Women In Film if it weren’t for that movie,” she said of the project that changed her life. Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF But ultimately, she’s enjoyed collaborating with women and exploring female characters. “I just love stories about women,” Wiig said. “We’re so crazy! We’re complex. We talk to each other about how we age, and our sensitivities and our intuition. It’s a never-ending source of material. I want to keep going,” she pledged. “I want to keep telling stories about women, with women.” Wiig then offered everyone a challenge. “I still have things in my career that I really want to do — that I’m really scared to do,” she confessed. “And so I just thought, by chance, if everyone in this room has that thing that they’ve really wanted to do or really been scared to do — maybe we make like a collective pact with each other that we’re going to just do it, anyway.” Don’t keep it to yourself…share the love! Offering game-changing shows like The Sopranos and The Wire , HBO became the creator-friendly destination that allowed original ideas to be explored with a level of quality previously unseen on network television. Some of the most important shows of the last few decades had a chance to flourish, but not all were so lucky. Whether it was due to low viewership or budgets that were impossible to sustain, a few intriguing shows couldn’t find their footing on the cable channel. These are ten canceled HBO shows that had all the potential to be great , but were unable to see their vision fully realized. For this list, we’ll only be looking at HBO originals, which will exclude any fantastic but short-lived MAX originals from making the cut. 10 \'The Nevers\' (2021) A woman in period clothing crouches down onto a road in The Nevers. Image via HBO The Nevers had an interesting premise and a talented cast and crew, but the series was unable to complete its first season. The Victorian-era series followed a group of individuals who find themselves with unique and extraordinary powers. Hunted and feared, these gifted few, known as the “touched,” must band together to operate in secret like steampunk superheroes. In an era where TV audiences are seeking new fantasy shows, The Nevers could have been the type of unique spin on the genre that developed a following . Unfortunately, the show’s creator, Joss Whedon, became persona non grata after accusations of workplace harassment from previous productions, and he would later step away from The Nevers while it was still filming. Only the first six episodes would air, and HBO canceled the series before finishing the season, a rare move for the cable channel. 9 \'The Franchise\' (2024) The production team of Maximum Studios\' "Tecto" watches their actors perform in \'The Franchise\'. Image via HBO HBO subscribers were able to peek into the fresh hell of blockbuster filmmaking with the short-lived comedy series The Franchise . The cast and crew of the superhero film Tecto: Eye of the Storm are doing their best to complete the production despite the fact that no one seems interested in the project. As daily problems besiege the set, First Assistant Director Daniel ( Himesh Patel ) is forced to find solutions to get the film wrapped. When The Franchise premiered, it was praised for its witty writing and attention to detail when satirizing the business of making superhero films. Considering the pedigree behind the camera that consisted of Jon Brown , Sam Mendes , and Armando Iannucci , expectations were high that the series would see at least a second season. Much to the disappointment of fans, The Franchise ended after one season with an open-ended finale , teeing up higher stakes and the possibility for interesting conflict that would never be realized. 8 \'Luck\' (2011–2012) Dennis Farina as Gus and Dustin Hoffman as Chester Berstein in Luck. Image via HBO A star-studded cast and a legendary television creator weren’t enough to keep Luck on track. Created by David Milch , Luck follows the many lives that intersect around the world of horse racing at a California racetrack. From the horse trainers in the stables to the gamblers who put their fates to the test, everyone has a story to tell and scores to settle on and off the track. The idea of seeing cinematic heavyweights like Dustin Hoffman and Nick Nolte chew scenery with Milch scripts was an exciting prospect. The show was critically praised, and HBO had announced a second season before later reversing the decision in light of on-set issues. Three horses had died during the production of Luck , and concern over the safety of animals led to the horse racing series finishing after only one lap. 7 \'Vinyl\' (2016) Ray Romano as Zak Yankovich in Vinyl Image via HBO Vinyl had all the makings of becoming HBO’s newest prestige hit, but the series unfortunately didn’t make it beyond one season. Set in the 1970s, Vinyl starred Bobby Cannavale as record executive Richie Finestra. Struggling to survive in a music industry beginning to change, Richie mounts a final effort to save his record label from becoming a casualty of new sounds and ideals. A show set in the music industry of the 70s offered opportunities for storylines that could have thrown the characters into real-life moments in history. However, even with names like Martin Scorsese and Mick Jagger attached as co-creators, Vinyl didn’t deliver ratings or enough critical favor to justify continuing the story . Although HBO was initially interested in producing a second season, it cut its losses after the ten episodes of season one. 6 \'Deadwood\' (2004–2007) Timothy Olyphant as Seth Bullock on \'Deadwood.\' Image via HBO It might seem strange to include a show that ran for three seasons, but Deadwood could have easily done twice that with more story left to tell. Set in the late 1800s, Deadwood brought viewers to the South Dakota gold mining camp of Deadwood. Established in a lawless territory, the residents of Deadwood searched for their fortunes before the land became an official part of the U.S. Even with only three seasons completed, Deadwood is considered by many as an essential Western show that should be watched by anyone who is a fan of the genre. Ian McShane , as the saloon owner Al Swearengen, is one of the greatest characters to appear on an HBO series, and the storylines defied what viewers expected from a typical western series. Budget concerns and a breakdown in communication between HBO and creator David Milch abruptly ended Deadwood at three seasons , but if viewers had known, at least a few would have kicked in a donation to keep the western on TV. \u200b\u200b\u200b 5 \'Lovecraft Country\' (2020) Leti stands outside in Lovecraft Country. Image via HBO For all the positive attention the series received, it’s still surprising that Lovecraft Country only produced one season. Set in the 1950s, Lovecraft Country follows Atticus ( Jonathan Majors ) as he searches for his missing father. Joining him is his friend Leticia ( Jurnee Smollett ) and his Uncle George ( Courtney B. Vance) as they encounter strange and horrific entities on their missing persons quest. HBO has experimented with many genres, but horror was mainly overlooked and limited to the anthology series Tales From the Crypt . Lovecraft Country promised to be an intelligent piece of horror that also examined relevant social issues , but the first season was also its last. Speculation regarding the cancelation varied from budgetary issues to an unclear path forward to a second season, but allegations about a toxic work environment on the Lovecraft Country set have also been mentioned regarding the unique and short-lived series. 4 \'Carnivàle\' (2003–2005) Justin stands next to a tattooed man in Carnivale. Image via HBO Carnivàle was a twisted and challenging gothic drama that failed to find an audience before its potential could be realized. Set during the Great Depression, Carnivàle told the story of two men, a runaway prisoner named Ben Hawkins ( Nick Stahl ), and a humble but conflicted Minister, Justin Crowe ( Clancy Brown ). While Justin grows his flock, Ben travels with a mystical carnival, each man destined to clash with the other in an epic showdown. Carnivàle was a narratively dense but rewarding show for those who stuck with it, constantly leaving viewers guessing as to what would happen next. Creator Daniel Knauf planned a story that would stretch over six seasons, but the dark fantasy series was cut short after two seasons. A combination of production costs and low viewership motivated HBO to make the decision, but fans will always wonder how the haunting and mysterious series would have played out under different circumstances. 3 \'Enlightened\' (2011–2013) Laura Dern as Amy with a shocked expression wearing a yellow top in \'Enlightened\' Image via HBO Fans of the dramedy Enlightened know there was a great deal of life left in the show. In Enlightened , Laura Dern stars as Amy Jellicoe, an abrasive executive who succumbs to a very public and career-damaging nervous breakdown. After returning from a wellness retreat, Amy attempts to approach her life from a calmer, more enlightened perspective, but practice proves harder than theory. Enlightened creator Mike White would later find massive success with The White Lotus , but drawing viewers to the Dern-led series proved too challenging. Although Enlightened boasted a strong performance from the ever-reliable Dern and struck a chord with the audience who tuned in, the viewing numbers were slim, even by prestige television standards . White had plans for what would happen to Amy if a third season were to take place, but Enlightened would be canceled after two seasons. 2 \'Rome\' (2005–2007) Ray Stevenson and Kevin McKidd as Roman soldiers standing alongside together in Rome (2005-2007). Image via HBO Rome was an ambitious period piece for HBO to attempt, but circumstances limited the series to a two-season run. Set in Ancient Rome, the series mixed historical events with fictional characters to give a dramatized view of Rome transitioning from a republic into an expansive empire. Rome was widely praised for its talented performances, unique approach to storytelling, and its epic scale. Truly, the word epic might be underselling it a bit, because the production quality in Rome was as if a big-budget blockbuster had been broken into episodic form for television . While the large-scale recreation of Rome was impressive, it was also expensive, and therein lay the obstacle to the show’s long-term success. A period show is already an expensive proposition, but the budget needed for Rome almost guaranteed the drama had no chance at being profitable. 1 \'Perry Mason\' (2020–2023) Matthew Rhys as Perry Mason in a suits and hat looks troubled standing outside in Perry Mason. Image via HBO In a perfect world, Perry Mason would still be churning out new seasons, but we’ll have to settle for the two we received. Before Perry Mason ( Matthew Rhys ) became a respected Defense Attorney, he was an investigator doing small-time jobs after returning from World War I. Perry is lost and looking for direction, but a sensational murder case will be the catalyst for him to embrace the next step of his career. HBO’s take on the famed fictional defense attorney was a moody, beautiful piece of noir , and Rhys’ performance was heartbreaking in its world weariness. Perry Mason was originally conceived as a miniseries, but the positive reception led to HBO picking up the drama as a regular series with a second season. Fortunes turn fast on television, though, and although no specific reason was cited, it’s assumed that lower viewership and production costs led to Perry Mason being canceled after two seasons. perry-mason-tv-poster.jpg Like perry mason Crime Release Date 2020 - 2023-00-00 Network HBO Max Cast See All Matthew Rhys Juliet Rylance Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming BUY Showrunner Jack Amiel Genres Crime Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. From broadly comedic whodunits to slow-burning thrillers with high stakes, Apple TV has a number of crime shows to satisfy fans of the genre. The following list covers eight of the best crime shows on Apple TV , each featuring enough murder, destruction, or robberies to keep a precinct of hardened detectives busy for the next year. 8 'Dope Thief' (2025) Brian Tyree Henry as Ray with Wagner Moura as Manny as they reel back in shock in Dope Thief. Image via Apple TV+ In Dope Thief , two friends, Ray ( Brian Tyree Henry ) and Manny ( Wagner Moura ), pose as DEA agents to rob drug houses. The plan seems like an easy enough con that won’t trace back to them, but the pair manages to draw attention from both sides of the law. In over their heads and with no one to trust, Ray and Manny will have to act carefully if they hope to survive an ordeal of their own creation. Dope Thief is beautifully shot, with cinematic visuals that make the series look more like a film than a television series. Henry and Moura’s performances are the driving force of Dope Thief , and their struggle to remain loyal to one another despite the challenges they face elevates the series past a standard crime show. Those viewers looking for a fast-paced series probably won’t find it in Dope Thief , but an audience looking for strong character work will enjoy the eight episodes. 7 'The Afterparty' (2022–2023) Ben Schwartz and Sam Richardson in The Afterparty Image via Apple TV+ The after-party of a high school reunion becomes a crime scene in the Apple murder mystery comedy The Afterparty . Pop star Xavier ( Dave Franco ) went from host to corpse in a matter of hours, and while the guests get their stories straight, the overzealous Detective Danner ( Tiffany Haddish ) sees this as a case that could make her career. Danner begins taking statements from the possible suspects, and although their stories are wildly different, a bigger picture leading to the culprit starts to form. The Afterparty is the perfect farcical murder mystery comedy ideal for fans of movies like Clue . The format of the series, where each episode is a different person’s perspective of the night’s events, avoids the trap of becoming repetitive by hiding enough clues in a story told by its reliably unreliable narrator. Each season of The Afterparty focuses on a new case with a few returning characters, but each cast is packed with comedic talent such as Sam Richardson , Zach Woods , and Ilana Glazer , making sure the improvisational-sounding flow of the comedy is consistently smooth and sharp. 6 'Smoke' (2025–Current) 'Dave Gudsen looking intently to his left in Smoke. Image via Apple TV+ Smoke follows police detective Michelle Calderone ( Jurnee Smollett ) and arson investigator Dave Gudsen ( Taron Egerton ) as they attempt to track down two serial arsonists. Gudsen balks at having Calderone assigned to his case, but soon, a mutual respect grows between the two. However, each has personal demons that factor into their investigation — demons that could likely put them on opposite sides as more details come to light. The point of view of our arsonists, the horrific damage they cause, and the enjoyment they receive from it leads to some truly creepy moments that will stick in the mind for days afterward. Egerton and Smollett play off one another well, and as their relationship continues to change over the nine episodes, we see the two investigators wordlessly switch tactics with one another, making for a compelling watch. When the plot twists in Smoke land, they drastically impact the story and guarantee the “Next Episode’ button is getting pressed. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 5 'Presumed Innocent' (2024–Current) Rusty is being led away in handcuffs in court with Raymond following in Presumed Innocent. Image via Apple TV+ The murder of an assistant prosecuting attorney becomes an even bigger scandal when the Chief Deputy Prosecutor is named the prime suspect. Presumed Innocent follows Rusty Sabich ( Jake Gyllenhaal ) as he is arrested and tried for the murder of his colleague, Carolyn Polhemus ( Renate Reinsve ), with whom he was having an affair. As the court case drags shameful secrets into the light, Rusty will find it increasingly difficult to prove his innocence. Even for those familiar with the original novel of the same name by Scott Turow or the 1990 film adaptation starring Harrison Ford , the TV version of Presumed Innocent will offer new plot twists to keep viewers engaged. Gyllenhaal shines as a man grappling with guilt about his involvement with the victim , but there’s no weak link in the phenomenal cast that includes Ruth Negga as his wife, Barbara, and Bill Camp as his former boss-turned-legal counsel, Raymond Horgan. The second season of Presumed Innocent will shift the series into an anthology format with a new case to follow, but anyone looking for a quick binge will receive a complete story with Season 1. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 4 'Bad Monkey' (2024–Current) Vince Vaughn sitting in a beach chair with a drink in Bad Monkey Episode 1. Image via Apple TV+ In Bad Monkey , Andrew Yancy ( Vince Vaughn ) was a great police detective who became a fairly apathetic health inspector after an altercation that put him in hot water. The arrival of a severed arm pulls Yancy back into some unofficial police work, and the fast-talking health inspector finds himself the target of some dangerous and increasingly desperate individuals. In the off chance Yancy can keep his personal life under control, he has a fighting chance of repairing his professional life if he can avoid getting killed in the process. Based on the novel of the same name by Carl Hiaasen, Bad Monkey allows its characters to be playful and get lost in banter while never losing sight of the murder mystery or the stakes of the case. Bad Monkey is the best balance of comedy and crime currently on Apple TV , and with a lead like Vaughn, who can keep one foot in both genres easily, it's a series that lends itself to substantial longevity on the streamer. The second season of Bad Monkey promises to give Yancy new co-stars to tangle with , which is one more reason to be excited for the return of the likable series. 3 'Your Friends & Neighbors' (2025–Current) A man goes from the envy of his upper-class community to the person breaking into their homes in Your Friends & Neighbors . Andrew “Coop” Cooper ( Jon Hamm ) is still emotionally reeling after the divorce from his wife, Mel ( Amanda Peet ), when he loses his job as a prominent hedge fund manager. Jaded from his recent failures and disillusioned by the wealth he sees around him, Coop begins to steal from the people he once thought of as friends. However, entering their homes allows Coop access to more than their valuables — he also discovers secrets they would kill to protect. Your Friends & Neighbors wisely relied on the charm and dry comedic ability of Hamm in the early stages of its story, but the series slowly built an interesting world around him. By the end of Season 1, many of the supporting characters were fully fleshed out into people who could carry side plots, which will only stand to make the show better. The end of Season 1 left many questions about how Coop moves forward with his life in light of major decisions, so it will be intriguing to see what his next steps are and how they impact his family, friends… and neighbors for Season 2. 2 'Criminal Record' (2024–Current) Cush Jumbo and Peter Capaldi standing beside each other in Criminal Record Image via Apple TV+ New details about an old murder case pit two detectives against one another in Criminal Record . An anonymous phone call leads Detective Sergeant June Lenker ( Cush Jumbo ) to believe an innocent man might be in jail for a murder he didn’t commit. June’s attempts to uncover the truth are blocked by Detective Chief Inspector Daniel Hegarty ( Peter Capaldi ), who believes firmly that the case in question should remain closed. When neither detective backs down, a professional disagreement quickly becomes personal. Criminal Record is one of Apple TV’s best crime offerings, loaded with the type of expertly laid out plot twists and tense drama that are the recipe for addictive television. Capaldi and Jumbo create a unique antagonistic chemistry that puts a fresh spin on a procedural mystery thriller, where the more they outmaneuver one another, the deeper their respect and will to succeed grow. With a confirmed second season of Criminal Record on the way, now is a great time to catch up before June and Daniel are back on the case. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 1 'Black Bird' (2022) James in on a payphone in prison in Black Bird. Image via Apple TV+ In the intense and thrilling miniseries Black Bird , Jimmy (Taron Egerton) is a small-time crook given a once-in-a-lifetime chance to commute his 10-year sentence. The prize is great, and so is the challenge: Jimmy must befriend fellow inmate Larry Hall ( Paul Walter Hauser ) with the goal of getting a confession about suspected murders. Larry is distrustful, guards are dangerous, and Jimmy doesn’t have much time before the offer expires. Egerton takes Jimmy from arrogant to honorable with no false moments, and Hauser rightfully won an Emmy by making Larry one of the most unnerving characters on television that year. There are moments of Black Bird that become so uncomfortably tense that it’s not uncommon to feel tired after watching an episode . That’s said as the highest form of compliment, because the story continues to raise the stakes scene by scene via a masterful combination of writing and acting, making Black Bird the easiest recommendation for fans of any genre. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The ideals of camp have evolved over time as our greatest creative minds have cracked open new ways to tell stories . What hasn't changed is the roots of the style and how they still play an important role in cinema. Though the campy stylings we saw back in the '70s are quite different from what we see today, camp is still alive and well. Over the past 10 years, campy films have risen to the top of the pack through comedy, drama, and horror , some of which have already secured a place in the conversation for future camp classics. Since 2015, we've had some really fabulous entries, but these 15 are pure camp . Maybe they were unintentionally campy, like House of Gucci , or inherently campy, like The Happytime Murders . Nevertheless, these films are wonderfully campy and deserve to be on your watch list. 15 'Joker: Folie à Deux' (2024) The Joker and Harley singing together in 'Joker Folie à Deux' Image via Warner Bros. Pictures There was absolutely nothing in Joker: Folie à Deux that was intended to be campy, but Todd Phillips ' execution made it a disastrous comedic romp. A dreamlike jukebox musical legal drama, the Joker sequel was a misguided, confused superhero offshoot that used a well-known character to create an absolutely gratuitous mess. And there, my friends, is why Joker: Foile a Deux is a bona fide camp classic. A stunning visual exploration, the film follows Arthur Fleck ( Joaquin Phoenix ) at Arkham State Hospital as he awaits trial for the crimes depicted in the previous film. As it gets closer to the day, he develops a romantic relationship with another inmate, Harley “Lee” Quinzel ( Lady Gaga ). With much anticipation for its release, the film had an underwhelming performance at the box office as it failed to meet expectations. With a theatrical sensibility, it’s become a camp masterpiece. Perhaps if it had embraced its elements rather than attempting to deliver its intent, audiences would have accepted it for what it was. Instead, it halted any forward motion for a franchise. Perhaps the only saving grace about this film is that we got some new Lady Gaga bangers out of it! 14 'Friendship' (2024) Tim Robinson giving a suspicious look while seated at a drum kit in Friendship Image via A24 There is an abundance of styles under the umbrella of comedy. Not every comedy is going to make you roll on the floor laughing; some are meant to make you laugh uncomfortably. If there is one actor who personifies that, it’s Tim Robinson . As a comedian who is finally getting his flowers, one of the projects that elicits uncomfortable laughter is Friendship . Written and directed by Andrew DeYoung , Friendship tells the story of extremely socially awkward Craig, a down-on-his-luck marketing executive, and his increasingly fraught connection with his new neighbor, Austin ( Paul Rudd ), a local TV meteorologist. As friendship leads to obsession, Craig’s already downward-spiraling life is about to reach rock bottom. Robinson is perfect in this role. In fact, the part was specifically written with him in mind . Unlike some other entries in this list, the humor is meant to be uncomfortable. You’re almost willed to watch through your fingers as things get increasingly worse for Craig. We tend to see Rudd as the funny one in films, but his darker turn here lends to the stressful humor. Even Kate Mara ’s wickedly unaware, despondent wife makes you cringe. And that’s where the camp comes in. Tapping into a different aesthetic makes Friendship an artistically sufficient cringe comedy. 13 'The Happytime Murders' (2018) Melissa McCarthy and her puppet partner in The Happytime Murders Image via STX Films I will forever consider Melissa McCarthy one of the greatest comedic actresses of our generation. Her body of work in comedies is extraordinary, guaranteeing laughs in nearly everything she does. Easily her campiest film to date, McCarthy pairs up with puppets for the buddy cop crime comedy The Happytime Murders . In a universe in which humans and puppets co-exist, puppet private investigator Phil Phillips ( Bill Barretta ) and human police detective Connie Edwards (McCarthy) must solve a murder spree of retired sitcom stars from the 1980s puppet show The Happytime Gang. Normally, I’d say no puppets were harmed during the filming, but that would be a lie. Despite the puppets, this is not a movie meant for kids. The humor is absolutely adult-oriented. The Happytime Murders is high-concept camp that is littered with crude jokes, satire, and graphic violence. You know exactly what’s in store when the logline is, “Sex. Murder. Puppets.” Despite the awful Rotten Tomatoes score , the reaction is likely from individuals who didn’t appreciate Brian Henson ’s vision. This is not The Muppets that his father turned into beloved household names. The Happytime Murders is a whole new way of puppeteering. If you love shock value, this movie is perfect for you. 12 'Freaky' (2020) Vince Vaughn standing in a school hallway with Misha Osherovich and Celeste O'Connor in Freaky (2020) Image via Universal Pictures Though some might consider Freaky Friday as the ultimate body-swapping comedy of the 21st century, there have been a few that have tested its title since its release. One such film is the comedy slasher flick Freaky . A twist on the aforementioned story, Freaky watches as Millie Kessler ( Kathryn Newton ), a tormented high school student, unintentionally switches bodies with the Blissfield Butcher ( Vince Vaughn ), an aging serial killer known as an urban legend in the town. As freaky deaky as the hilarious movie is, it’s pure camp. Just look at Vaughn’s performance! It’s one of the best and most underrated in his later career. Freaky is essentially a mashup of Scream and Freaky Friday with a touch of tongue-in-cheek humor. Christopher Landon , who also directed Happy Death Day , employs a horror-comedy style that melds the genres seamlessly in this underseen smash. 11 'Free Guy' (2021) Ryan Reynolds as Guy in Free Guy Image via 20th Century Studios It’s absolutely wild that the guy who once starred in Two Guys, a Girl, and a Pizza Place has become a mega Hollywood star who owns a soccer club and a mobile company. But that’s our timeline! Ryan Reynolds has played many action heroes in his illustrious career, but when he took on the leading role in Free Guy , he proved, once again, that he can do literally anything. Shawn Levy ’s Free Guy brings the video game world to life as it shares the tale of Guy (Reynolds), a bank teller, who discovers that he is a non-player character in a massively multiplayer online game , who then partners with player and unemployed software designer Millie Rusk ( Jodie Comer ) to find evidence that a gaming company's CEO stole the source code of the player's game. The universe Free Guy creates is absolutely bonkers. Levy drops us into this digital world while establishing the film as a high-octane action film . The film pays homage to the games we adore playing while also openly mocking and parodying them. Reynolds' performance is simply charming and endearing. Even Comer’s performance as a certified action star pairs well with Reynolds, playing the straight guy to Guy. Free Guy is a blast of a film. Its silliness, paired with its over-the-top sincerity, makes it a wonderful camp movie. 10 'Birds of Prey' (2020) Image via Warner Bros. Let’s get it out of the way: Margot Robbie as Harley Quinn is perfection. The moment she stepped inside the DCEU, superhero movies changed forever. Her colorful and whimsical portrayal of the crazed criminal and Joker’s girlfriend changed our perception forever. As the definitive Harley Quinn, we all wanted more, and so we were given a sequel to Suicide Squad called Birds of Prey . A girl power-forward film, Birds of Prey finds a single Harley being threatened by Gotham City crime lord Roman Sionis ( Ewan McGregor ) and joins forces with Helena Bertinelli ( Mary Elizabeth Winstead ), Dinah Lance ( Jurnee Smollett-Bell ), and Renee Montoya ( Rosie Perez ) to save Cassandra Cain. With a flamboyant palette and a lighthearted, irreverent tone, Birds of Prey is as fun as it is an action thriller. Though its predecessor and subsequent follow-up use a similar tone, Birds of Prey stands out as a camp classic because it assures the female solidarity that’s central to the film. We’ve seen kickass female heroes and women, but it’s a rarity to see them team up in this manner without a male character taking over. The fresh perspective on superhero films was too much for some fanatics, which is a shame. Birds of Prey will always have a place in my heart. 9 'Bottoms' (2023) Ayo Edebiri and Rachel Sennott looking confused in Bottoms Image via MGM Bottoms follows two high school seniors, PJ ( Rachel Sennott ) and Josie ( Ayo Edebiri ), who happen to be “untalented gays,” who start a fight club as a way to hook up with cheerleaders. Absurd and wildly over-the-top, Bottoms is like if Bring It On and But I’m a Cheerleader had a Gen Z baby. Emma Seligman and Sennott created a surreal, over-the-top high school in which satire keeps the focus on raunchy, unapologetic, and irreverent themes. Though it is an homage to teen sex comedies of the past, Bottoms is unapologetically revelatory. By igniting the comedy through a queer lens, Bottoms naturally fits the mold of a camp film, but its ability to appeal to a wider audience speaks to its style and accessibility. With a generation proudly questioning their identity and sexuality, Bottoms provides a safe place to laugh and ponder simultaneously. If you watched in real time or are coming at it fresh today, it’s now automatically campy to see Kaia Garber, Nicholas Galitzine , and Edibori go completely ham. With a wonderfully nostalgic tone, Bottoms is destined to become a future camp classic. 8 'House of Gucci' (2021) Lady Gaga as Patrizia Reggiani standing in the snow in ski gear and smiling in House of Gucci Image via United Artists Releasing I know what you’re thinking. How is House of Gucci a campy film? I urge you to go back and watch. From the costumes to the accents, from Jared Leto to everything Lady Gaga does on screen, House of Gucci is a whirlwind of everything you could ever desire . The Ridley Scott film is more than just a biographical crime drama — it’s an experience. The film is a dramatized retelling of the Gucci family, focusing on Patrizia Reggiani (Lady Gaga) and Maurizio Gucci ( Adam Driver ). From marriage to an acrimonious divorce, driven by Patrizia's ambition and the family's internal struggles over the fashion empire, the crime comes alive as Patrizia orchestrates her ex-husband’s murder. With a cast that also includes Al Pacino and Jeremy Irons , House of Gucci was an ambitious undertaking to say the least. With both fact and fiction colliding through artistic liberties, if you take House of Gucci for what it is, it’s an absolute delight. You might even wonder if Ryan Murphy was a part of its creation. Now, to the cons. The problem with the film is that its tonal shifts are poorly played. They don’t mesh well, causing the uneven storytelling to veer into the camp world. Though played completely straight, everything about House of Gucci is actually quite exaggerated , and we’re all better for it. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 7 'Bodies Bodies Bodies' (2022) Amandla Stenberg, Maria Bakalova, Chase Sui Wonders, and Rachel Sennott covered in blood in Bodies Bodies Bodies Image via A24 Horror comedies are innately camp. When a horror comedy finds the balance between storytelling and style, it becomes something worthwhile. In Bodies Bodies Bodies , audiences are taken on a wild adventure through friendship and murder with unexpected moments along the way. The brilliantly hilarious film follows a group of friends reuniting at a remote mansion. As they are stranded during a hurricane, they kill time by playing a murder-in-the-dark style party game that results in an actual dead body and a whole lot of lies and deception. With a killer among them, Bodies Bodies Bodies is about truth and survival. A hyper-stylized film, Bodies Bodies Bodies is more than just a silly thriller — it’s filled with a brilliant discussion of class, privilege, and generational culture. Imagine an Agatha Christie mystery with a modern lens, and that’s what this film exudes. There are over-the-top moments and characters that bring out genuine laughter alongside those moments of uncomfortable chuckles. The film also holds a mirror up to Gen-Z’s politically correct beliefs about image and perception , where trust and loyalty are almost instantly tossed out the window. The movie is a bloody good time. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 6 'Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar' (2021) Kristen Wiig and Annie Mumolo in Barb & Star Go to Vista Del Mar Image via Lionsgate/Cate Cameron If the title alone doesn’t scream camp, I don’t know what does! Written and starring Kristen Wiig and Annie Mumolo , reuniting after working on Bridesmaids together, Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar tells the story of two lifelong best friends from the Midwest who leave their small town for the first time to go on vacation in Florida, where they get mixed up in a villain's plot to kill everyone in town. With an ensemble that includes stellar performances from Jamie Dornan, Damon Wayans, Wendi McClendon-Covey, Vanessa Bayer , and more, this absurdly funny flick is a brightly colored delight. The plot is goofy, mixing its comedy with its thrills , and it finds the campy balance needed. The leading ladies have an exuberant amount of fun delivering the funny. And yes, we have permission to laugh at the accents. For a film that was forced to have a streaming release, Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar received enough love through word of mouth that it became a quick hit. Surely, there’s a universe in which Barb and Star get a sequel! Google is updating how content is shown. Horror fans have been eating well this last decade on streaming television, with a lot of horror hits coming out on Netflix, HBO, and Amazon Prime Video. HBO Max, in particular, has been bringing the scares . The Last of Us , True Blood , The Outsider , and now It: Welcome to Derry are all massively popular TV shows and great examples of how to do long-form horror. Lovecraft Country should be added to this list as well. Lovecraft Country Is A Horrifying, Entertaining Series Lovecraft Country is a wildly unique horror series, and while it does include some of the mind-melting beasts courtesy of the show\'s namesake, like shoggoths and Cthulu, it\'s not an adaptation of any one H.P. story. Instead, it\'s an adaptation of Matt Ruff\'s 2016 horror novel. The series is set in 1950s Jim Crow America and follows Tic Freeman (Jonathan Majors) and Leti Lewis (Jurnee Smollett) as they embark on a dangerous road trip through some of the most racist parts of the country. They meet horrors beyond their comprehension, and bring them back to Chicago with them. While the monsters, witches, and ghosts are plenty terrifying, it\'s the violent racism they face day in and day out that puts them most at peril. Lovecraft Country is a beautifully directed show with fantastical ideas mixed in elegantly with the issues of segregation and prejudice, making for a terrifying and thoughtful experiment. Lovecraft Country Was Canceled After One Season Despite Great Reviews Lovecraft Country ran for 10 episodes, and it felt like the series had plenty of ideas for more seasons to come, but in July 2021, HBO announced that they were canceling the series (via Deadline ). HBO simply said, " We will not be moving forward with a second season of Lovecraft Country ." While Lovecraft Country season 1 had a book to go off, showrunner Misha Green and her team had to craft an original story for season 2. It sounds like HBO gave Green and her team some time to think up a new season, but ultimately decided that they would be canceling the show instead. Lovecraft Country was slow to grow, but once it did, it had significant viewing numbers. The season finale hit a viewership high with 1.5 M, becoming the most-watched new episode of an HBO Max original series in its first day. On Friday night, Nicky Zimmermann and Simone Zimmermann hosted a star-studded dinner at Chateau Marmont to celebrate the Australian brand’s cruise 2026 collection, “Twisted Romance.” The new collection is inspired by “nostalgia, femininity, and the fantasy of escape,” and the glamorous celebration reflected the same feeling. Guests, including Zoey Deutch, Jurnee Smollett, and Emma Roberts, were treated to a candlelit dinner in the famed hotel’s Bungalow, at tables set with antique candelabras, strings of pearls, and lush greenery. Stefanie Keenan // Getty Images Emma Roberts before dinner. Following dinner, guests headed upstairs to the Chateau Marmont’s Penthouse for dancing and continued festivities, complete with a set by DJ Kitty Kash. WWD // Getty Images DJ Kitty Kash manning the turntable. “Cruise 26 is inspired by nostalgic pirate adventures and the flamboyance of the New Romantics,” said Nicky in a statement on the new collection. “A treasure trove of nostalgia is given fresh interpretation through fluid fabrics, dynamic shapes and illustrative prints to capture a carefree mood.” The creative director continued, “We played a lot with contrast—floaty silks against structured denim, delicate lace paired with sharp tailoring. There’s volume, romance, and drama, but it’s never too serious. That tension is what makes it feel modern: celebrating a sense of fun, freedom and a little rebellious adventure.” Stefanie Keenan // Getty Images Nina Garcia and Bella Heathcote. The invite list included some of the biggest names in Hollywood, all of them wearing pieces from the collection, including Dakota Fanning, Rita Ora, Halle Bailey, Delaney Rowe, Isabela Merced, Bella Heathcote, Maria Bakalova, Abby Champion, and more. ELLE’s editor-in-chief Nina Garcia was also in attendance. Scroll through the gallery below for a glimpse inside the evening. But it had been a while since Nicky and Simone Zimmermann had dropped into Los Angeles, where they opened their first-ever Stateside boutique back in 2011. (There are now some 92 standalone stores scattered across the globe.) Arriving to some very un-SoCal-like rain and flash flood warnings, the intense weather didn’t dampen the sisters’ perennially upbeat Aussie nature. Indeed, the bizarre conditions made for even more of a surreal and cinematic night at the fabled Chateau Marmont to celebrate the Twisted Romance-themed Cruise 2026 collection. Although rainwater was practically ricocheting off the neon sign erected poolside as a step-and-repeat photo moment, it didn’t deter guests from pulling their best blue steel poses, showing off their outfits for awaiting DJ-turned-photographer Myles Hendrik. As such, the best accessory of the evening proved to be a personal umbrella-wielding gentleman, ensuring no one slid right off the soaking wet tree-lined pathways. Once dried off indoors, attendees warmed up in glow of the Chateau’s candlelit bungalow over dirty martinis, glasses of Champagne, and deep belly laughter. Model Abby Champion, who has walked countless Zimmermann runways and recently wore a custom dress by Nicky Zimmermann during her wedding weekend , reunited with the Sydney-based designer. Longtime friends Emma Roberts, Dakota Fanning, and Zoey Deutch giggled together in a corner, while Jurnee Smollett introduced Halle Bailey to her older sister, Jazz. A long and languorous dinner unfolded at ethereal tables that nodded to the Twisted Romance mood. Ivory linens were laden with candelabras, deep burgundy-hued calla lilies, old silver coins, strings of pearls, and vintage glassware: an aesthetically-pleasing backdrop for crowd-favorite dishes like spicy tuna tartare, beetroot salad, Mediterranean branzino, and roasted chicken. “Tonight is about reconnecting with you all,” Nicky said, fresh from Paris where she splits her time to oversee the design atelier. “We haven't been going through LA as much as we used to, and we're lucky we get to see a lot of you around the world. Our first store in the US was on Robertson, which, like many things in our lives, came to us by chance and luck. We’ve now been in business nearly 35 years—which feels like a miracle! There’s a lot of stylists here, and we want you to know that your support is so meaningful and it has contributed a huge amount. We have always found LA, in particular, to be so supportive of us.” As anyone who owns a Zimmermann frock will tell you, they’re not pieces made for just sitting idle in. Before the last dinner fork had even hit the scallop-edged plate, guests were starting to make their way through the hotel to Penthouse 64 where the promise of dancing awaited. A corseted and ruffle-adorned Kitty Cash was already manning the DJ decks, and antique silver trays of espresso martinis were easily finding their way into outstretched hands. Actress Maria Bakalova was so relaxed, she was yapping cross-legged on the floor beside the fireplace, while the terrace became the place to grab both a chocolate madeline and a Vogue cigarette. With the rain pelting down on Sunset Boulevard and the wide open possibility of a Friday night ahead, there was simply no good reason to leave. Word travels fast too, as certain A listers who had been staying at the hotel for the GQ Men of the Year bash the night previous, caught wind and stopped by to hangout until well after 2 a.m. “I had no idea the Zimmermanns were this fun,” Rita Ora could be heard remarking. “It makes me love the clothes even more now.” Photo by: Myles Hendrik 1/18 Rita Ora Photo by: Myles Hendrik 2/18 Abby Champion, Larsen Thompson, Chloe East Photo by: Myles Hendrik 3/18 Beatrice Grannò Photo by: Myles Hendrik 4/18 Zoey Deutch, Dakota Fanning Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images 5/18 Emma Roberts More from Vogue Kate Middleton’s Dazzling Chandelier Earrings Are Steeped in Royal History Gather ’Round! Carter, Colleen Atwood), fashion (Anthony Vaccarello, Zac Posen, Jerry Lorenzo) and other power players in Anna Wintour’s orbit (Gov. Gavin Newsom, Bryan Lourd, Tyler Perry, Casey Wasserman) strolled past props, costume rails and spotlights on their way to director’s chair seats. The runway was high-energy and fast — people were having fun! — which is something we need more of in fashion and worked well for the 35-minute livestream of the show. While it was confusing to figure out what was designer-made and what was costume, that may have been the point. Damson Idris and Angela Bassett walk the runway at Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty The art forms have blurred. Costume designers have dipped their toes into fashion design and collaborated with luxury brands on films, not to mention continually influencing runway and street style decade after decade. Meanwhile, fashion designers are casting Hollywood faces as brand ambassadors, bringing even more showmanship to their runway shows and clothing to reach digital audiences, and even stepping into producing and costuming Hollywood films. All of it was on display on the runway. L.A.-based designers Kate and Laura Mulleavy were working in both worlds long before Anthony Vaccarello and Saint Laurent Films began producing awards-contending movies. They designed costumes for the 2010 film “Black Swan,” have cited the influence of films including “Suspiria” and “Star Wars” on many of their runway collections over the years, and made their own 2017 feature film, “Woodshock.” So it was fitting that several of their looks appeared on the Vogue World runway. Kendall Jenner wears a costume from “Moulin Rouge!,” a model wears a dress by Rodarte, Doja Cat wears a costume by Michael Schmidt inspired by Tina Turner in “Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome.” Source: Getty There used to be more of an impervious line between Hollywood costume and fashion; costume was for character building and serving a script, fashion was purely commercial. But all that’s gone out the window, as the relationship between Hollywood and fashion has become symbiotic. “In this era, people are able to step out of the boxes more and interact in the two fields simultaneously, and it’s accepted and celebrated,” Laura Mulleavy told me, noting that it was another polymath, Shirley Kurata, their longtime runway stylist and the costume designer for the 2022 film “Everything Everywhere All At Once,” who curated the evening’s contemporary character costumes. Jeff Goldblum walks the runway wearing Gucci at Vogue World. Source: Getty This recognition of costume designers’ contributions to visual culture — and to fashion, including countless collection mood boards — was long overdue. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve previewed a collection with a fashion designer who talks about being inspired by a particular film without naming, or even knowing, the costume designer. Hopefully, that mindset will start to change. The photo below says it all about the flow of creativity and reference from one world to the other — Wintour poses with costume designer Mona May and her iconic yellow plaid suit, as worn by Alicia Silverstone in the 1995 film “Clueless,” alongside a checked suit in the same spirit by fashion designer Thom Browne. Left to right, a model wears Thom Browne, costume designer Mona May, Condé Nast Chief Content Director Anna Wintour and a Mona May-designed costume from Clueless. Source: Getty There was a lot to look at on the runway. Some of the highlights: Kendall Jenner as a “Moulin Rouge!” showgirl in a leggy look from costume designer Catherine Martin, and “Great Gatsby” flappers — including Elizabeth Debicki — wearing beaded gowns Martin created for the 2013 film in collaboration with Prada. The tribute to the late, great style icon Diane Keaton and her influential “Annie Hall” look was not only touching but telling of how costume and fashion can intersect. It was originally developed by Keaton in 1977 with costume designer Ruth Morley, using some pieces from her personal wardrobe and some from Ralph Lauren, who recreated the look for the runway here, and has referenced it many times in his fashion collections over the years. There were also homages to the unforgettable costumes of “The Royal Tenenbaums” (Karen Patch), “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” (Arianne Phillips) and “Edward Scissorhands” (Colleen Atwood). Elizabeth Debicki wallks the runway at Vogue World. Source: Getty Angela Bassett closed the Afrofuturism section looking regal in her Ruth E. Carter gown on the heels of dancing “Black Panther” Wakandan warriors. Greta Lee worked a theatrical look and tricorne hat from fashion/costume designer Jonathan Anderson’s first Dior collection shown just weeks ago. Jeff Goldblum owned his Gucci sequin jacket and his runway walk, and Julia Garner skipped down the runway as the picture of baroque frivolity in a Milena Canonero for “Marie Antoinette” costume. Julia Garner walks the runway at Vogue World. It was a blast and nobody wanted it to end. On the way out, I ran into “Frankenstein” costume designer Kate Hawley, whose ravishing work, including curating Tiffany & Co. archival jewels and custom pieces for the film, is proof that the love affair between costume and fashion isn’t ending anytime soon. Everything from Boucheron jewels and hot-off-the-runway Versace to designer Camilla Franks’ fun, rock ’n’ roll resortwear and Le Monde Beryl’s red-carpet-ready silk pumps is being showcased for celebrities and stylists at spectacular events, rented hotel rooms and showrooms across the city. The goal? To create media moments, build relationships and make deals as opportunities to dress up, ramp up over the next few months. Swarovski joined the chorus Tuesday, asserting its role as chief embellisher of fashion and film. Global creative director Giovanna Engelbert and CEO Alexis Nasard hosted the opening of the Swarovski “Masters of Light” immersive exhibition — following stops in Vienna, Milan, Shanghai and Seoul — curated by Alexander Fury with a Hollywood focus for this edition. Unlike most fashion happenings, this is open to the public, through Nov. 3 in the former Amoeba Music space. Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie designed gown worn by Marilyn Monroe on display at Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood.” Source: Swarovski Cher, Viola Davis, Kylie Jenner, Elizabeth Olsen, Jeff Goldblum and many more turned out for the sparkly opening, exploring galleries showcasing Swarovski’s 130 year history of bedazzling fashion, jewelry, home decor and more. The brand has a century-long history in Hollywood, from lighting up Dorothy’s ruby red slippers in “The Wizard of Oz” (there’s a pair in the exhibition), to creating the jewels worn by Marilyn Monroe in “Gentlemen Prefer Blondes” (also here), to partnering with the Academy Awards, and on many a costume and red carpet dress. Like Vogue World, the exhibition is a conversation between fashion and costume — and full of eye candy — including the Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie-designed nude illusion dress worn by Monroe when she sang “Happy Birthday” to President John F. Kennedy, and by Kim Kardashian to the Met Gala, which had its own velvet-roped vestibule. Cher and Giovanna Battaglia Engelbert at the opening of Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood.” Source: Swarovski Demonstrating how costumes have inspired fashion, Travis Banton’s gold silk, glass bead, bullion, crystal and mink “Fabergé” dress — said to be one of the most expensive ever produced by Paramount and worn by Marlene Dietrich in the 1937 film “Angel” — is displayed next to a 2024 Marc Jacobs gown inspired by it. “Masters of Light” offers a window into the brand’s craft and design process in vivid color, and many more show stopping looks, including Josephine Baker’s incredible metal and crystal bra and feather costume from “La Revue Nègre,” Katy Perry’s iconic Jeremy Scott chandelier dress, a crystallized Harry Styles jumpsuit and more worn by Cher, Madonna, Grace Jones, Beyoncé, Tina Turner, Carey Mulligan and more. Source: Tory Burch All The Cool Girls… Former magazine editors Laura Brown and Kristina O’Neill have been crisscrossing the country with their new book, “All The Cool Girls Get Fired,” which I had the pleasure of interviewing them about onstage at Reese Witherspoon’s Shine Away event a couple weekends back. It’s a timely read for people who, ahem, have been laid off, with personal anecdotes from Oprah, Katie Couric, Jamie Lee Curtis and others, as well as practical advice about COBRA and mental health — all the fun stuff. Critics Choice Super Awards to Air This Weekend Sammi Turano November 12, 2025 Originally posted on January 6, 2021 @ 5:00 pm The Critics Choice Association (CCA) announced today the incredible line-up of talent that will join hosts Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the inaugural Critics Choice Super Awards , helping them to honor the most popular, fan-obsessed genres across both television and movies, including Superhero/Comic Book, Science Fiction/Fantasy, Horror, Action and Animation. Shohreh Aghdashloo, Aya Cash, Madelyn Cline, Mike Colter, Colman Domingo, Tom Ellis, Courtney Ford, Tiffany Haddish, Sam Heughan, Maddison Jaizani, Lennie James, Martin Kove, Javicia Leslie, Leah Lewis, Caity Lotz, Ralph Macchio, Kennedy McMann, Elizabeth Mitchell, Lindsey Morgan, Bob Morley, Genevieve Padalecki, Jared Padalecki, Brandon Routh, Chase Stokes, Eliza Taylor, Gina Torres, Alan Tudyk, and William Zabka, will all serve as presenters during the special ceremony, which will air on The CW Network on Sunday, January 10, 2021 (8:00-10:00pm ET/PT) and will stream the next day for free on The CW App and cwtv.com. “We know that the Super Awards are in the best hands with Kevin Smith and Dani Fernandez at the helm,” said Critics Choice Association CEO Joey Berlin. “They bring with them an unparalleled knowledge of and enthusiasm for these sometimes underappreciated genres that we know fans and viewers will love. They are joined by a stellar line-up of fan favorites who will be on hand to support their ‘Super’ colleagues and help showcase the very best in popular entertainment.” The Critics Choice Association will also present the Legacy Award to the “Star Trek” franchise, recognizing the cultural impact it has had across multiple decades while continuing to appeal to and grow its loyal fanbase with new stories and characters. “Star Trek” icon Patrick Stewart , and “Star Trek: Discovery” trailblazer Sonequa Martin-Green will personally accept this special honor, which comes as the franchise celebrates its 55 th anniversary. See also Critics Choice Association to Honor Harrison Ford Hulu and NEON’s “Palm Springs” leads this year’s film nominees, with a total of five including Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Andy Samberg, Best Actor in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie and Best Villain in a Movie for J.K. Simmons, and Best Actress in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Movie for Cristin Milioti. Several films followed close behind with four nominations including “Birds of Prey” (Warner Bros.), “Freaky” (Universal), “Onward” (Disney+), “Sonic the Hedgehog” (Paramount), “The Hunt” (Universal), “The Old Guard” (Netflix), and “The Willoughbys” (Netflix). “Lovecraft Country” (HBO) received the most television nominations, with a total of six possible wins, including Best Horror Series, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Jonathan Majors, Best Actor in a Horror Series for Michael K. Williams, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Wunmi Mosaku, Best Actress in a Horror Series for Jurnee Smollett, and Best Villain in a Series for Abbey Lee. Amazon’s “The Boys” received five nominations including Best Superhero/Comic Book Series, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series and Best Villain in a Series for Antony Starr, Best Actor in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Karl Urban, and Best Actress in a Superhero/Comic Book Series for Aya Cash. For the full list of nominees, and additional information, visit: https://www.criticschoice.com/critics-choice-super-awards/ Kevin Smith has been saying silly cinematic shit since 1994’s “Clerks.” 2021 marks the 27 th year since the last time he had a real job. A polygamist, he’s married to both his wife, Jen, and podcasting. Writer, comedian, and actress Dani Fernandez is a frequent speaker at San Diego Comic Con, LA Comic Con, and New York Comic Con and has been a panelist for The CW’s “Crisis Aftermath.” She has hosted for E!, Disney, Nerdist, Skybound, Funimation, and iHeartRadio, among others. She can currently be seen on Syfy’s “The Great Debate” and in Disney’s “Ralph Breaks the Internet,” playing herself. She is also an accomplished television writer with credits at Netflix and HBO Max. See also Shirley Wins SOFEE The inaugural Critics Choice Super Awards show will be produced by Bob Bain Productions. The CCA is represented by Dan Black of Greenberg Traurig. She pulled back her maroon Max Mara blazer to reveal a black T-shirt with the word, “resist.” Fonda continued: “I realized, given today’s reality, humanitarianism and empathy are essential forms of resistance. … It’s at the heart of what we do in our profession, empathy. And you know what else is at the heart of what we do? The First Amendment. Our profession, like all art forms, can’t exist without freedom of expression. It’s the bedrock of democracy, and it’s being taken away from us. And that’s why, on Oct. 1, we launched the Committee for the First Amendment .” Fonda clarified the Committee was re-launched, as it existed in the ’70’s and ’80s, when her father was a member. “But dig this,” she said. “That was about one small part of government robbing us of our First Amendment. Right now, it’s the entire federal government. It is far, far worse than what existed back in the ’40s and ’50s. And so, we have to do something about that.” Then she praised the recipient of this year’s Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award. “Jamie Lee Curtis and I have a few things in common,” Fonda said. “We’re both children of major movie stars and we made our own way quite successfully in their business. And we’re both late bloomers — which is okay. It moves me very deeply to see how Jamie uses her skills and her remarkable ego-less courage as an actor. … And last January, when the fires were burning and our hearts were breaking, I heard Jamie Lee Curtis had given a million dollars to the fire department and it made me cry.” Fonda added how Curtis had also raised millions of dollars for Children’s Hospital L.A., and has used her voice for addiction and trans rights. When she took the stage, Curtis also spoke about government. “I heard it today that she is retiring from public service, and I thought this Women In Film crowd could just give Nancy Pelosi a loud [round of applause]. … What an example to me of a life of service!” She also professed: “I am most excited to stand here two days after the repudiation of the authoritative regime. The election of these two beautiful women to governorships.” Curtis thanked her presenter. “Jane Fonda, I have watched you in wonder and shock and awe, at the way that you walk through the world as an artist, as an activist and as a disruptor in residence.” She noted that she joined the Committee of the First Amendment. Lastly, Kaia Gerber honored her Palm Royale co-star Kristen Wiig with the inaugural Icon Award. “Who better to receive it than my favorite scene partner?” Gerber said. “For seven years at SNL , Kristen showed us comedy could be completely unhinged and utterly ‘stupid’ — a word I learned from Kristen herself as one of the highest forms of praise in comedy — and also, somehow be simultaneously deeply human.” Kaia Gerber, Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF and Icon Award recipient Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Gerber continued, “When Bridesmaids came out, it was a revelation. … There is such truth and utter heartbreak behind [all of her characters].” She finished, “Tonight, we celebrate the woman who taught us that comedy is art, that chaos is beautiful, that sheer stupidity is not only encouraged but a necessity of life and that being unapologetically yourself might just be the most iconic move of all.” An emotional Wiig thanked Gerber, who she called “a lighthouse” on her show. “I’m fully overwhelmed,” she said. “This is my first time having to make a speech like this. I just kept thinking, ‘How did I get here?’ … I keep coming back to the people who said ‘yes’ to me before I had anything on my resume.” Wiig noted how her whole life changed when she joined The Groundlings. “That led to SNL ,” she said. She called out two men: Bridesmaids director Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow (who reached out to her and asked if she wanted to write something). “I certainly wouldn’t be up here getting an award from Women In Film if it weren’t for that movie,” she said of the project that changed her life. Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF But ultimately, she’s enjoyed collaborating with women and exploring female characters. “I just love stories about women,” Wiig said. “We’re so crazy! We’re complex. We talk to each other about how we age, and our sensitivities and our intuition. It’s a never-ending source of material. I want to keep going,” she pledged. “I want to keep telling stories about women, with women.” Wiig then offered everyone a challenge. “I still have things in my career that I really want to do — that I’m really scared to do,” she confessed. “And so I just thought, by chance, if everyone in this room has that thing that they’ve really wanted to do or really been scared to do — maybe we make like a collective pact with each other that we’re going to just do it, anyway.” Don’t keep it to yourself…share the love! Offering game-changing shows like The Sopranos and The Wire , HBO became the creator-friendly destination that allowed original ideas to be explored with a level of quality previously unseen on network television. Some of the most important shows of the last few decades had a chance to flourish, but not all were so lucky. Whether it was due to low viewership or budgets that were impossible to sustain, a few intriguing shows couldn’t find their footing on the cable channel. These are ten canceled HBO shows that had all the potential to be great , but were unable to see their vision fully realized. For this list, we’ll only be looking at HBO originals, which will exclude any fantastic but short-lived MAX originals from making the cut. 10 \'The Nevers\' (2021) A woman in period clothing crouches down onto a road in The Nevers. Image via HBO The Nevers had an interesting premise and a talented cast and crew, but the series was unable to complete its first season. The Victorian-era series followed a group of individuals who find themselves with unique and extraordinary powers. Hunted and feared, these gifted few, known as the “touched,” must band together to operate in secret like steampunk superheroes. In an era where TV audiences are seeking new fantasy shows, The Nevers could have been the type of unique spin on the genre that developed a following . Unfortunately, the show’s creator, Joss Whedon, became persona non grata after accusations of workplace harassment from previous productions, and he would later step away from The Nevers while it was still filming. Only the first six episodes would air, and HBO canceled the series before finishing the season, a rare move for the cable channel. 9 \'The Franchise\' (2024) The production team of Maximum Studios\' "Tecto" watches their actors perform in \'The Franchise\'. Image via HBO HBO subscribers were able to peek into the fresh hell of blockbuster filmmaking with the short-lived comedy series The Franchise . The cast and crew of the superhero film Tecto: Eye of the Storm are doing their best to complete the production despite the fact that no one seems interested in the project. As daily problems besiege the set, First Assistant Director Daniel ( Himesh Patel ) is forced to find solutions to get the film wrapped. When The Franchise premiered, it was praised for its witty writing and attention to detail when satirizing the business of making superhero films. Considering the pedigree behind the camera that consisted of Jon Brown , Sam Mendes , and Armando Iannucci , expectations were high that the series would see at least a second season. Much to the disappointment of fans, The Franchise ended after one season with an open-ended finale , teeing up higher stakes and the possibility for interesting conflict that would never be realized. 8 \'Luck\' (2011–2012) Dennis Farina as Gus and Dustin Hoffman as Chester Berstein in Luck. Image via HBO A star-studded cast and a legendary television creator weren’t enough to keep Luck on track. Created by David Milch , Luck follows the many lives that intersect around the world of horse racing at a California racetrack. From the horse trainers in the stables to the gamblers who put their fates to the test, everyone has a story to tell and scores to settle on and off the track. The idea of seeing cinematic heavyweights like Dustin Hoffman and Nick Nolte chew scenery with Milch scripts was an exciting prospect. The show was critically praised, and HBO had announced a second season before later reversing the decision in light of on-set issues. Three horses had died during the production of Luck , and concern over the safety of animals led to the horse racing series finishing after only one lap. 7 \'Vinyl\' (2016) Ray Romano as Zak Yankovich in Vinyl Image via HBO Vinyl had all the makings of becoming HBO’s newest prestige hit, but the series unfortunately didn’t make it beyond one season. Set in the 1970s, Vinyl starred Bobby Cannavale as record executive Richie Finestra. Struggling to survive in a music industry beginning to change, Richie mounts a final effort to save his record label from becoming a casualty of new sounds and ideals. A show set in the music industry of the 70s offered opportunities for storylines that could have thrown the characters into real-life moments in history. However, even with names like Martin Scorsese and Mick Jagger attached as co-creators, Vinyl didn’t deliver ratings or enough critical favor to justify continuing the story . Although HBO was initially interested in producing a second season, it cut its losses after the ten episodes of season one. 6 \'Deadwood\' (2004–2007) Timothy Olyphant as Seth Bullock on \'Deadwood.\' Image via HBO It might seem strange to include a show that ran for three seasons, but Deadwood could have easily done twice that with more story left to tell. Set in the late 1800s, Deadwood brought viewers to the South Dakota gold mining camp of Deadwood. Established in a lawless territory, the residents of Deadwood searched for their fortunes before the land became an official part of the U.S. Even with only three seasons completed, Deadwood is considered by many as an essential Western show that should be watched by anyone who is a fan of the genre. Ian McShane , as the saloon owner Al Swearengen, is one of the greatest characters to appear on an HBO series, and the storylines defied what viewers expected from a typical western series. Budget concerns and a breakdown in communication between HBO and creator David Milch abruptly ended Deadwood at three seasons , but if viewers had known, at least a few would have kicked in a donation to keep the western on TV. \u200b\u200b\u200b 5 \'Lovecraft Country\' (2020) Leti stands outside in Lovecraft Country. Image via HBO For all the positive attention the series received, it’s still surprising that Lovecraft Country only produced one season. Set in the 1950s, Lovecraft Country follows Atticus ( Jonathan Majors ) as he searches for his missing father. Joining him is his friend Leticia ( Jurnee Smollett ) and his Uncle George ( Courtney B. Vance) as they encounter strange and horrific entities on their missing persons quest. HBO has experimented with many genres, but horror was mainly overlooked and limited to the anthology series Tales From the Crypt . Lovecraft Country promised to be an intelligent piece of horror that also examined relevant social issues , but the first season was also its last. Speculation regarding the cancelation varied from budgetary issues to an unclear path forward to a second season, but allegations about a toxic work environment on the Lovecraft Country set have also been mentioned regarding the unique and short-lived series. 4 \'Carnivàle\' (2003–2005) Justin stands next to a tattooed man in Carnivale. Image via HBO Carnivàle was a twisted and challenging gothic drama that failed to find an audience before its potential could be realized. Set during the Great Depression, Carnivàle told the story of two men, a runaway prisoner named Ben Hawkins ( Nick Stahl ), and a humble but conflicted Minister, Justin Crowe ( Clancy Brown ). While Justin grows his flock, Ben travels with a mystical carnival, each man destined to clash with the other in an epic showdown. Carnivàle was a narratively dense but rewarding show for those who stuck with it, constantly leaving viewers guessing as to what would happen next. Creator Daniel Knauf planned a story that would stretch over six seasons, but the dark fantasy series was cut short after two seasons. A combination of production costs and low viewership motivated HBO to make the decision, but fans will always wonder how the haunting and mysterious series would have played out under different circumstances. 3 \'Enlightened\' (2011–2013) Laura Dern as Amy with a shocked expression wearing a yellow top in \'Enlightened\' Image via HBO Fans of the dramedy Enlightened know there was a great deal of life left in the show. In Enlightened , Laura Dern stars as Amy Jellicoe, an abrasive executive who succumbs to a very public and career-damaging nervous breakdown. After returning from a wellness retreat, Amy attempts to approach her life from a calmer, more enlightened perspective, but practice proves harder than theory. Enlightened creator Mike White would later find massive success with The White Lotus , but drawing viewers to the Dern-led series proved too challenging. Although Enlightened boasted a strong performance from the ever-reliable Dern and struck a chord with the audience who tuned in, the viewing numbers were slim, even by prestige television standards . White had plans for what would happen to Amy if a third season were to take place, but Enlightened would be canceled after two seasons. 2 \'Rome\' (2005–2007) Ray Stevenson and Kevin McKidd as Roman soldiers standing alongside together in Rome (2005-2007). Image via HBO Rome was an ambitious period piece for HBO to attempt, but circumstances limited the series to a two-season run. Set in Ancient Rome, the series mixed historical events with fictional characters to give a dramatized view of Rome transitioning from a republic into an expansive empire. Rome was widely praised for its talented performances, unique approach to storytelling, and its epic scale. Truly, the word epic might be underselling it a bit, because the production quality in Rome was as if a big-budget blockbuster had been broken into episodic form for television . While the large-scale recreation of Rome was impressive, it was also expensive, and therein lay the obstacle to the show’s long-term success. A period show is already an expensive proposition, but the budget needed for Rome almost guaranteed the drama had no chance at being profitable. 1 \'Perry Mason\' (2020–2023) Matthew Rhys as Perry Mason in a suits and hat looks troubled standing outside in Perry Mason. Image via HBO In a perfect world, Perry Mason would still be churning out new seasons, but we’ll have to settle for the two we received. Before Perry Mason ( Matthew Rhys ) became a respected Defense Attorney, he was an investigator doing small-time jobs after returning from World War I. Perry is lost and looking for direction, but a sensational murder case will be the catalyst for him to embrace the next step of his career. HBO’s take on the famed fictional defense attorney was a moody, beautiful piece of noir , and Rhys’ performance was heartbreaking in its world weariness. Perry Mason was originally conceived as a miniseries, but the positive reception led to HBO picking up the drama as a regular series with a second season. Fortunes turn fast on television, though, and although no specific reason was cited, it’s assumed that lower viewership and production costs led to Perry Mason being canceled after two seasons. perry-mason-tv-poster.jpg Like perry mason Crime Release Date 2020 - 2023-00-00 Network HBO Max Cast See All Matthew Rhys Juliet Rylance Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming BUY Showrunner Jack Amiel Genres Crime Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown.
