Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200bIn a relatively short period of time, Apple TV has established itself as a streamer with quality original programming . From the feel-good comedy Ted Lasso to the sci-fi dark mystery Severance , Apple TV covers the spectrum of tastes. The same can be said for their varied offering of crime shows. From broadly comedic whodunits to slow-burning thrillers with high stakes, Apple TV has a number of crime shows to satisfy fans of the genre. The following list covers eight of the best crime shows on Apple TV , each featuring enough murder, destruction, or robberies to keep a precinct of hardened detectives busy for the next year. 8 'Dope Thief' (2025) Brian Tyree Henry as Ray with Wagner Moura as Manny as they reel back in shock in Dope Thief. Image via Apple TV+ In Dope Thief , two friends, Ray ( Brian Tyree Henry ) and Manny ( Wagner Moura ), pose as DEA agents to rob drug houses. The plan seems like an easy enough con that won’t trace back to them, but the pair manages to draw attention from both sides of the law. In over their heads and with no one to trust, Ray and Manny will have to act carefully if they hope to survive an ordeal of their own creation. Dope Thief is beautifully shot, with cinematic visuals that make the series look more like a film than a television series. Henry and Moura’s performances are the driving force of Dope Thief , and their struggle to remain loyal to one another despite the challenges they face elevates the series past a standard crime show. Those viewers looking for a fast-paced series probably won’t find it in Dope Thief , but an audience looking for strong character work will enjoy the eight episodes. 7 'The Afterparty' (2022–2023) Ben Schwartz and Sam Richardson in The Afterparty Image via Apple TV+ The after-party of a high school reunion becomes a crime scene in the Apple murder mystery comedy The Afterparty . Pop star Xavier ( Dave Franco ) went from host to corpse in a matter of hours, and while the guests get their stories straight, the overzealous Detective Danner ( Tiffany Haddish ) sees this as a case that could make her career. Danner begins taking statements from the possible suspects, and although their stories are wildly different, a bigger picture leading to the culprit starts to form. The Afterparty is the perfect farcical murder mystery comedy ideal for fans of movies like Clue . The format of the series, where each episode is a different person’s perspective of the night’s events, avoids the trap of becoming repetitive by hiding enough clues in a story told by its reliably unreliable narrator. Each season of The Afterparty focuses on a new case with a few returning characters, but each cast is packed with comedic talent such as Sam Richardson , Zach Woods , and Ilana Glazer , making sure the improvisational-sounding flow of the comedy is consistently smooth and sharp. 6 'Smoke' (2025–Current) 'Dave Gudsen looking intently to his left in Smoke. Image via Apple TV+ Smoke follows police detective Michelle Calderone ( Jurnee Smollett ) and arson investigator Dave Gudsen ( Taron Egerton ) as they attempt to track down two serial arsonists. Gudsen balks at having Calderone assigned to his case, but soon, a mutual respect grows between the two. However, each has personal demons that factor into their investigation — demons that could likely put them on opposite sides as more details come to light. The point of view of our arsonists, the horrific damage they cause, and the enjoyment they receive from it leads to some truly creepy moments that will stick in the mind for days afterward. Egerton and Smollett play off one another well, and as their relationship continues to change over the nine episodes, we see the two investigators wordlessly switch tactics with one another, making for a compelling watch. When the plot twists in Smoke land, they drastically impact the story and guarantee the “Next Episode’ button is getting pressed. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 5 'Presumed Innocent' (2024–Current) Rusty is being led away in handcuffs in court with Raymond following in Presumed Innocent. Image via Apple TV+ The murder of an assistant prosecuting attorney becomes an even bigger scandal when the Chief Deputy Prosecutor is named the prime suspect. Presumed Innocent follows Rusty Sabich ( Jake Gyllenhaal ) as he is arrested and tried for the murder of his colleague, Carolyn Polhemus ( Renate Reinsve ), with whom he was having an affair. As the court case drags shameful secrets into the light, Rusty will find it increasingly difficult to prove his innocence. Even for those familiar with the original novel of the same name by Scott Turow or the 1990 film adaptation starring Harrison Ford , the TV version of Presumed Innocent will offer new plot twists to keep viewers engaged. Gyllenhaal shines as a man grappling with guilt about his involvement with the victim , but there’s no weak link in the phenomenal cast that includes Ruth Negga as his wife, Barbara, and Bill Camp as his former boss-turned-legal counsel, Raymond Horgan. The second season of Presumed Innocent will shift the series into an anthology format with a new case to follow, but anyone looking for a quick binge will receive a complete story with Season 1. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 4 'Bad Monkey' (2024–Current) Vince Vaughn sitting in a beach chair with a drink in Bad Monkey Episode 1. Image via Apple TV+ In Bad Monkey , Andrew Yancy ( Vince Vaughn ) was a great police detective who became a fairly apathetic health inspector after an altercation that put him in hot water. The arrival of a severed arm pulls Yancy back into some unofficial police work, and the fast-talking health inspector finds himself the target of some dangerous and increasingly desperate individuals. In the off chance Yancy can keep his personal life under control, he has a fighting chance of repairing his professional life if he can avoid getting killed in the process. Based on the novel of the same name by Carl Hiaasen, Bad Monkey allows its characters to be playful and get lost in banter while never losing sight of the murder mystery or the stakes of the case. Bad Monkey is the best balance of comedy and crime currently on Apple TV , and with a lead like Vaughn, who can keep one foot in both genres easily, it's a series that lends itself to substantial longevity on the streamer. The second season of Bad Monkey promises to give Yancy new co-stars to tangle with , which is one more reason to be excited for the return of the likable series. 3 'Your Friends & Neighbors' (2025–Current) A man goes from the envy of his upper-class community to the person breaking into their homes in Your Friends & Neighbors . Andrew “Coop” Cooper ( Jon Hamm ) is still emotionally reeling after the divorce from his wife, Mel ( Amanda Peet ), when he loses his job as a prominent hedge fund manager. Jaded from his recent failures and disillusioned by the wealth he sees around him, Coop begins to steal from the people he once thought of as friends. However, entering their homes allows Coop access to more than their valuables — he also discovers secrets they would kill to protect. Your Friends & Neighbors wisely relied on the charm and dry comedic ability of Hamm in the early stages of its story, but the series slowly built an interesting world around him. By the end of Season 1, many of the supporting characters were fully fleshed out into people who could carry side plots, which will only stand to make the show better. The end of Season 1 left many questions about how Coop moves forward with his life in light of major decisions, so it will be intriguing to see what his next steps are and how they impact his family, friends… and neighbors for Season 2. 2 'Criminal Record' (2024–Current) Cush Jumbo and Peter Capaldi standing beside each other in Criminal Record Image via Apple TV+ New details about an old murder case pit two detectives against one another in Criminal Record . An anonymous phone call leads Detective Sergeant June Lenker ( Cush Jumbo ) to believe an innocent man might be in jail for a murder he didn’t commit. June’s attempts to uncover the truth are blocked by Detective Chief Inspector Daniel Hegarty ( Peter Capaldi ), who believes firmly that the case in question should remain closed. When neither detective backs down, a professional disagreement quickly becomes personal. Criminal Record is one of Apple TV’s best crime offerings, loaded with the type of expertly laid out plot twists and tense drama that are the recipe for addictive television. Capaldi and Jumbo create a unique antagonistic chemistry that puts a fresh spin on a procedural mystery thriller, where the more they outmaneuver one another, the deeper their respect and will to succeed grow. With a confirmed second season of Criminal Record on the way, now is a great time to catch up before June and Daniel are back on the case. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 1 'Black Bird' (2022) James in on a payphone in prison in Black Bird. Image via Apple TV+ In the intense and thrilling miniseries Black Bird , Jimmy (Taron Egerton) is a small-time crook given a once-in-a-lifetime chance to commute his 10-year sentence. The prize is great, and so is the challenge: Jimmy must befriend fellow inmate Larry Hall ( Paul Walter Hauser ) with the goal of getting a confession about suspected murders. Larry is distrustful, guards are dangerous, and Jimmy doesn’t have much time before the offer expires. Egerton takes Jimmy from arrogant to honorable with no false moments, and Hauser rightfully won an Emmy by making Larry one of the most unnerving characters on television that year. There are moments of Black Bird that become so uncomfortably tense that it’s not uncommon to feel tired after watching an episode . That’s said as the highest form of compliment, because the story continues to raise the stakes scene by scene via a masterful combination of writing and acting, making Black Bird the easiest recommendation for fans of any genre. What hasn't changed is the roots of the style and how they still play an important role in cinema. Though the campy stylings we saw back in the '70s are quite different from what we see today, camp is still alive and well. Over the past 10 years, campy films have risen to the top of the pack through comedy, drama, and horror , some of which have already secured a place in the conversation for future camp classics. Since 2015, we've had some really fabulous entries, but these 15 are pure camp . Maybe they were unintentionally campy, like House of Gucci , or inherently campy, like The Happytime Murders . Nevertheless, these films are wonderfully campy and deserve to be on your watch list. 15 'Joker: Folie à Deux' (2024) The Joker and Harley singing together in 'Joker Folie à Deux' Image via Warner Bros. Pictures There was absolutely nothing in Joker: Folie à Deux that was intended to be campy, but Todd Phillips ' execution made it a disastrous comedic romp. A dreamlike jukebox musical legal drama, the Joker sequel was a misguided, confused superhero offshoot that used a well-known character to create an absolutely gratuitous mess. And there, my friends, is why Joker: Foile a Deux is a bona fide camp classic. A stunning visual exploration, the film follows Arthur Fleck ( Joaquin Phoenix ) at Arkham State Hospital as he awaits trial for the crimes depicted in the previous film. As it gets closer to the day, he develops a romantic relationship with another inmate, Harley “Lee” Quinzel ( Lady Gaga ). With much anticipation for its release, the film had an underwhelming performance at the box office as it failed to meet expectations. With a theatrical sensibility, it’s become a camp masterpiece. Perhaps if it had embraced its elements rather than attempting to deliver its intent, audiences would have accepted it for what it was. Instead, it halted any forward motion for a franchise. Perhaps the only saving grace about this film is that we got some new Lady Gaga bangers out of it! 14 'Friendship' (2024) Tim Robinson giving a suspicious look while seated at a drum kit in Friendship Image via A24 There is an abundance of styles under the umbrella of comedy. Not every comedy is going to make you roll on the floor laughing; some are meant to make you laugh uncomfortably. If there is one actor who personifies that, it’s Tim Robinson . As a comedian who is finally getting his flowers, one of the projects that elicits uncomfortable laughter is Friendship . Written and directed by Andrew DeYoung , Friendship tells the story of extremely socially awkward Craig, a down-on-his-luck marketing executive, and his increasingly fraught connection with his new neighbor, Austin ( Paul Rudd ), a local TV meteorologist. As friendship leads to obsession, Craig’s already downward-spiraling life is about to reach rock bottom. Robinson is perfect in this role. In fact, the part was specifically written with him in mind . Unlike some other entries in this list, the humor is meant to be uncomfortable. You’re almost willed to watch through your fingers as things get increasingly worse for Craig. We tend to see Rudd as the funny one in films, but his darker turn here lends to the stressful humor. Even Kate Mara ’s wickedly unaware, despondent wife makes you cringe. And that’s where the camp comes in. Tapping into a different aesthetic makes Friendship an artistically sufficient cringe comedy. 13 'The Happytime Murders' (2018) Melissa McCarthy and her puppet partner in The Happytime Murders Image via STX Films I will forever consider Melissa McCarthy one of the greatest comedic actresses of our generation. Her body of work in comedies is extraordinary, guaranteeing laughs in nearly everything she does. Easily her campiest film to date, McCarthy pairs up with puppets for the buddy cop crime comedy The Happytime Murders . In a universe in which humans and puppets co-exist, puppet private investigator Phil Phillips ( Bill Barretta ) and human police detective Connie Edwards (McCarthy) must solve a murder spree of retired sitcom stars from the 1980s puppet show The Happytime Gang. Normally, I’d say no puppets were harmed during the filming, but that would be a lie. Despite the puppets, this is not a movie meant for kids. The humor is absolutely adult-oriented. The Happytime Murders is high-concept camp that is littered with crude jokes, satire, and graphic violence. You know exactly what’s in store when the logline is, “Sex. Murder. Puppets.” Despite the awful Rotten Tomatoes score , the reaction is likely from individuals who didn’t appreciate Brian Henson ’s vision. This is not The Muppets that his father turned into beloved household names. The Happytime Murders is a whole new way of puppeteering. If you love shock value, this movie is perfect for you. 12 'Freaky' (2020) Vince Vaughn standing in a school hallway with Misha Osherovich and Celeste O'Connor in Freaky (2020) Image via Universal Pictures Though some might consider Freaky Friday as the ultimate body-swapping comedy of the 21st century, there have been a few that have tested its title since its release. One such film is the comedy slasher flick Freaky . A twist on the aforementioned story, Freaky watches as Millie Kessler ( Kathryn Newton ), a tormented high school student, unintentionally switches bodies with the Blissfield Butcher ( Vince Vaughn ), an aging serial killer known as an urban legend in the town. As freaky deaky as the hilarious movie is, it’s pure camp. Just look at Vaughn’s performance! It’s one of the best and most underrated in his later career. Freaky is essentially a mashup of Scream and Freaky Friday with a touch of tongue-in-cheek humor. Christopher Landon , who also directed Happy Death Day , employs a horror-comedy style that melds the genres seamlessly in this underseen smash. 11 'Free Guy' (2021) Ryan Reynolds as Guy in Free Guy Image via 20th Century Studios It’s absolutely wild that the guy who once starred in Two Guys, a Girl, and a Pizza Place has become a mega Hollywood star who owns a soccer club and a mobile company. But that’s our timeline! Ryan Reynolds has played many action heroes in his illustrious career, but when he took on the leading role in Free Guy , he proved, once again, that he can do literally anything. Shawn Levy ’s Free Guy brings the video game world to life as it shares the tale of Guy (Reynolds), a bank teller, who discovers that he is a non-player character in a massively multiplayer online game , who then partners with player and unemployed software designer Millie Rusk ( Jodie Comer ) to find evidence that a gaming company's CEO stole the source code of the player's game. The universe Free Guy creates is absolutely bonkers. Levy drops us into this digital world while establishing the film as a high-octane action film . The film pays homage to the games we adore playing while also openly mocking and parodying them. Reynolds' performance is simply charming and endearing. Even Comer’s performance as a certified action star pairs well with Reynolds, playing the straight guy to Guy. Free Guy is a blast of a film. Its silliness, paired with its over-the-top sincerity, makes it a wonderful camp movie. 10 'Birds of Prey' (2020) Image via Warner Bros. Let’s get it out of the way: Margot Robbie as Harley Quinn is perfection. The moment she stepped inside the DCEU, superhero movies changed forever. Her colorful and whimsical portrayal of the crazed criminal and Joker’s girlfriend changed our perception forever. As the definitive Harley Quinn, we all wanted more, and so we were given a sequel to Suicide Squad called Birds of Prey . A girl power-forward film, Birds of Prey finds a single Harley being threatened by Gotham City crime lord Roman Sionis ( Ewan McGregor ) and joins forces with Helena Bertinelli ( Mary Elizabeth Winstead ), Dinah Lance ( Jurnee Smollett-Bell ), and Renee Montoya ( Rosie Perez ) to save Cassandra Cain. With a flamboyant palette and a lighthearted, irreverent tone, Birds of Prey is as fun as it is an action thriller. Though its predecessor and subsequent follow-up use a similar tone, Birds of Prey stands out as a camp classic because it assures the female solidarity that’s central to the film. We’ve seen kickass female heroes and women, but it’s a rarity to see them team up in this manner without a male character taking over. The fresh perspective on superhero films was too much for some fanatics, which is a shame. Birds of Prey will always have a place in my heart. 9 'Bottoms' (2023) Ayo Edebiri and Rachel Sennott looking confused in Bottoms Image via MGM Bottoms follows two high school seniors, PJ ( Rachel Sennott ) and Josie ( Ayo Edebiri ), who happen to be “untalented gays,” who start a fight club as a way to hook up with cheerleaders. Absurd and wildly over-the-top, Bottoms is like if Bring It On and But I’m a Cheerleader had a Gen Z baby. Emma Seligman and Sennott created a surreal, over-the-top high school in which satire keeps the focus on raunchy, unapologetic, and irreverent themes. Though it is an homage to teen sex comedies of the past, Bottoms is unapologetically revelatory. By igniting the comedy through a queer lens, Bottoms naturally fits the mold of a camp film, but its ability to appeal to a wider audience speaks to its style and accessibility. With a generation proudly questioning their identity and sexuality, Bottoms provides a safe place to laugh and ponder simultaneously. If you watched in real time or are coming at it fresh today, it’s now automatically campy to see Kaia Garber, Nicholas Galitzine , and Edibori go completely ham. With a wonderfully nostalgic tone, Bottoms is destined to become a future camp classic. 8 'House of Gucci' (2021) Lady Gaga as Patrizia Reggiani standing in the snow in ski gear and smiling in House of Gucci Image via United Artists Releasing I know what you’re thinking. How is House of Gucci a campy film? I urge you to go back and watch. From the costumes to the accents, from Jared Leto to everything Lady Gaga does on screen, House of Gucci is a whirlwind of everything you could ever desire . The Ridley Scott film is more than just a biographical crime drama — it’s an experience. The film is a dramatized retelling of the Gucci family, focusing on Patrizia Reggiani (Lady Gaga) and Maurizio Gucci ( Adam Driver ). From marriage to an acrimonious divorce, driven by Patrizia's ambition and the family's internal struggles over the fashion empire, the crime comes alive as Patrizia orchestrates her ex-husband’s murder. With a cast that also includes Al Pacino and Jeremy Irons , House of Gucci was an ambitious undertaking to say the least. With both fact and fiction colliding through artistic liberties, if you take House of Gucci for what it is, it’s an absolute delight. You might even wonder if Ryan Murphy was a part of its creation. Now, to the cons. The problem with the film is that its tonal shifts are poorly played. They don’t mesh well, causing the uneven storytelling to veer into the camp world. Though played completely straight, everything about House of Gucci is actually quite exaggerated , and we’re all better for it. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 7 'Bodies Bodies Bodies' (2022) Amandla Stenberg, Maria Bakalova, Chase Sui Wonders, and Rachel Sennott covered in blood in Bodies Bodies Bodies Image via A24 Horror comedies are innately camp. When a horror comedy finds the balance between storytelling and style, it becomes something worthwhile. In Bodies Bodies Bodies , audiences are taken on a wild adventure through friendship and murder with unexpected moments along the way. The brilliantly hilarious film follows a group of friends reuniting at a remote mansion. As they are stranded during a hurricane, they kill time by playing a murder-in-the-dark style party game that results in an actual dead body and a whole lot of lies and deception. With a killer among them, Bodies Bodies Bodies is about truth and survival. A hyper-stylized film, Bodies Bodies Bodies is more than just a silly thriller — it’s filled with a brilliant discussion of class, privilege, and generational culture. Imagine an Agatha Christie mystery with a modern lens, and that’s what this film exudes. There are over-the-top moments and characters that bring out genuine laughter alongside those moments of uncomfortable chuckles. The film also holds a mirror up to Gen-Z’s politically correct beliefs about image and perception , where trust and loyalty are almost instantly tossed out the window. The movie is a bloody good time. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 6 'Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar' (2021) Kristen Wiig and Annie Mumolo in Barb & Star Go to Vista Del Mar Image via Lionsgate/Cate Cameron If the title alone doesn’t scream camp, I don’t know what does! Written and starring Kristen Wiig and Annie Mumolo , reuniting after working on Bridesmaids together, Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar tells the story of two lifelong best friends from the Midwest who leave their small town for the first time to go on vacation in Florida, where they get mixed up in a villain's plot to kill everyone in town. With an ensemble that includes stellar performances from Jamie Dornan, Damon Wayans, Wendi McClendon-Covey, Vanessa Bayer , and more, this absurdly funny flick is a brightly colored delight. The plot is goofy, mixing its comedy with its thrills , and it finds the campy balance needed. The leading ladies have an exuberant amount of fun delivering the funny. And yes, we have permission to laugh at the accents. For a film that was forced to have a streaming release, Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar received enough love through word of mouth that it became a quick hit. Surely, there’s a universe in which Barb and Star get a sequel! Google is updating how content is shown. From her early days in teen dramas to her breakout roles in musical comedies and emotionally resonant movies and TV series, she has consistently shown that she can slip into any character with ease . Whether she\'s delivering sharp comedic timing, heartfelt vulnerability, or powerhouse vocals, Snow brings a warmth and relatability that has made audiences root for her for more than two decades. As an artist, Snow has chosen projects that span genres including rom-coms, thrillers, ensemble musicals, and dramas. This range has made it difficult for fans to pick just one definitive "best" performance, because she shines in so many different ways. Still, a handful of movies and TV shows stand out as milestones in her career, shaping her identity as one of Hollywood\'s most consistently compelling talents. The best Brittany Snow projects highlight her ability to leave a lasting impression whether in a leading role or as part of a larger ensemble . 10 \'Crazy Ex Girlfriend\' (2015–2019) A closeup of Brittany Snow looking at the camera and talking in Crazy Ex Girlfriend. Image via The CW Crazy Ex-Girlfriend is a musical comedy-drama that follows Rebecca Bunch ( Rachel Bloom ), a high-powered but unhappy New York lawyer who impulsively moves to West Covina, California, after a chance encounter with her childhood crush, Josh Chan ( Vincent Rodriguez III ). What begins as a romantic quest quickly becomes a deeper exploration of mental health, identity, and the pursuit of happiness . Snow plays Josh\'s girlfriend Anna Hicks, who is introduced in the series\' second season. While this is a recurring role, Snow\'s character in Crazy Ex-Girlfriend immediately makes an impact because she subverts the expectations of a "mean girl". Snow brings a perfect balance of over-the-top arrogance and subtle vulnerability to a character who is a star from the background. Crazy Ex-Girlfriend is also a musical comedy, and Snow’s performance showcased her vocal chops . Songs like "Research Me Obsessively" allowed her to combine humor, musicality, and storytelling in a way that few of her previous roles demanded. 9 \'The Beast in Me\' (2025–) Brittany Snow in a tan blazer staring ahead in The Beast in Me. Image via Netflix The Beast in Me is a psychological thriller series that introduces Aggie Wiggs ( Claire Danes ), a successful author who’s been paralyzed by grief after the death of her young son. After finding herself unable to write, her life takes a dark turn when Nile Jarvis ( Matthew Rhys ), a wealthy real estate heir with a secretive past, moves in next door. As Aggie becomes obsessed with his story, she embarks on a dangerous game of cat-and-mouse . Snow plays Nina Jarvis, Nile\'s second wife. Brittany Snow stands out in The Beast in Me because she\'s able to subvert the expectations of what many would expect of a "wife" character. This is a darker, more dramatic role than many of the others she\'s known for. Although Nina isn\'t a central character in this story, Snow makes her stand out and makes it clear that she\'s never to be underestimated . In particular, Snow portrays her as someone with something to hide and her own motivations that make her a potential threat to those around her. 8 \'Someone Great\' (2019) Blair (Brittany Snow) asking for party drugs on the way to Neon Classic in Someone Great. Image via Netflix Someone Great is a romantic comedy that follows Jenny ( Gina Rodriguez ), a music journalist in New York City who lands her dream job in San Francisco, only to be heartbroken when her boyfriend of nine years, Nate ( LaKeith Stanfield ), breaks up with her. Reeling from the breakup, Jenny leans on her two best friends, Erin ( DeWanda Wise ) and Blair ( Brittany Snow ), to take her on one last wild day in the city . They skip work, party, chase concert tickets, and confront big life decisions that they\'ve been putting off. Someone Great gives Snow a chance to showcase how well she\'s able to shine in a strong ensemble. This movie isn’t just a fairy-tale rom‑com. Instead, it tackles real heartbreak, life transitions, and self-discovery. Snow is able to tap into Blair\'s humanity and highlight the fact that she\'s trying to navigate these tough issues with nuance and grace . Blair is exactly the type of character that Snow is so perfectly suited to play, since she\'s sweet, funny, and just trying to do the best she can. 7 \'American Dreams\' (2002–2005) Brittany Snow and the cast of American Dreams standing together in front of their home. Image via NBC American Dreams is a period drama set in 1960s Philadelphia. The series introduces the Pryor family, who do their best to navigate the seismic cultural shifts of the era. The show specifically follows Meg Pryor (Snow), a teenage girl whose dream is to dance on American Bandstand , and her journey growing up amid political unrest, civil rights struggles, and the Vietnam War . Alongside her, her brothers, parents, and friends deal with changing gender roles, racism, war, and social upheaval. American Dreams is one of Snow\'s most notable series since it was one of her first major TV roles . She convincingly captures the plight of a teenage girl growing up in the 1960s in America navigating ambition, family challenges, and social change. Meg evolves from a dream-filled teen into a young woman confronting real-world issues like prejudice, war, and personal responsibility, allowing Snow to play both lighthearted and deeply emotional scenes. This is an early look at Snow\'s talents and how she was able to shine from the earliest days of her career. 6 \'Pitch Perfect\' (2012) Pitch Perfect is a musical comedy that introduces Beca ( Anna Kendrick ), a college freshman with a passion for music, who reluctantly joins the Barden University a cappella group, the Bellas . The all-female group, mocked for their outdated style and internal conflicts, struggles to regain their former glory in the competitive world of collegiate a cappella. The Bellas are co-led by Chloe Beale (Snow), who recognizes that the group needs Beca\'s talent if they want a chance of succeeding. Pitch Perfect is one of Snow\'s best movies because it allowed her to showcase a mix of talents that play to her strengths, including acting, singing, and comedic timing, all in a single role. Snow\'s charm and stage presence help balance the movie\'s musical performances with its comedic and emotional moments . Additionally, Pitch Perfect \'s popularity and cult status gave her career a big boost, making it one of her most memorable and defining roles. 5 \'Hairspray\' (2007) Zac Efron and Brittany Snow in \'Hairspray\' Image via New Line Cinema Hairspray is a musical comedy set in 1960s Baltimore that follows Tracy Turnblad ( Nikki Blonsky ), a spirited and plus-sized teenager with big dreams of dancing on a local TV dance show. When she lands a spot on the program, Tracy uses her newfound fame to challenge the show\'s racial segregation and fight for integration. Snow plays Amber Von Tussle, the lead female dancer on "The Corny Collins Show" who feels threatened by Tracy\'s talent . Hairspray stands out as one of Snow\'s best movies because it gives her a chance to be a compelling villain to root against . More than being a bratty teenager, she represents the worst parts of American society with her attitude of entitlement and refusal to consider anyone other than herself. Snow fully leans into the camp and charisma needed for the role, making Amber both entertaining and memorable rather than a one-note villain. 4 \'John Tucker Must Die\' (2006) Brittany Snow as Kate looking at someone and smiling in John Tucker Must Die. Image via 20th Century Studios John Tucker Must Die is a teen comedy about three popular high-school girls who discover they\'ve all been secretly dating the same charming but manipulative basketball star, John Tucker ( Jesse Metcalfe ). Furious, they recruit a shy new girl, Kate (Snow), to help them take him down by transforming her into his dream girl and then publicly breaking his heart . Their revenge plans escalate and include everything ranging from embarrassing pranks to emotional sabotage. John Tucker Must Die is one of Brittany Snow\'s best movies because it showcases her strengths as a comedic and relatable leading actress . Snow brings sincerity, great timing, and a sweet vulnerability to this role, which is essential to the story\'s over-the-top antics. John Tucker Must Die gives her space to be funny, charming, and emotionally compelling all at once, and her performance helps elevate the ensemble that makes the movie so enjoyable. 3 \'X\' (2022) Brittany Snow in a red jumpsuit rests by a gas pump with a cameraman nearby in X. Image via A24 X is a slasher-horror movie set in 1979 that follows a small group of aspiring filmmakers who rent a rural Texas farmhouse to secretly shoot an adult film. The elderly owners, Pearl ( Mia Goth ) and Howard ( Stephen Ure ), seem odd but harmless at first, until Pearl becomes fixated on the youth and sexuality of the visitors, triggering a violent, nightmarish killing spree . Snow plays Bobby-Lynne, a burlesque dancer who is trying her best to build a career. X is one of Brittany Snow\'s best movies because it lets her step outside the wholesome or comedic roles she\'s most associated with and delivers a bold, memorable performance in a gritty horror setting. As Bobby-Lynne, she brings charisma, humor, and surprising emotional depth to a character who could\'ve been forgettable . Snow balances confidence and vulnerability in a way that makes Bobby-Lynne stand out within the ensemble and her presence adds levity and heart to a movie that\'s otherwise dark and intense. 2 \'The Hunting Wives\' (2025–) Malin Akerman as Margo teaches Brittany Snow as Sophie to fire a gun in the pilot of The Hunting Wives. Image via Netflix The Hunting Wives follows Sophie O\'Neill (Snow), a woman who leaves behind her busy Chicago life for what she hopes will be a quieter, more fulfilling existence in the small town of Mapleton, Texas. There she becomes entangled with a seductive, privileged social circle led by the magnetic and manipulative Margot Banks ( Malin Akerman ). The group\'s glamorous façade hides darker obsessions. The Hunting Wives follows these women as they party, host secret shooting outings, and engage in increasingly reckless behavior. The Hunting Wives is one of Brittany Snow\'s standout projects, not just because of her performance, but because of the way the series combines psychological suspense with social drama . Sophie\'s transformation from outsider to someone entangled in dark, morally ambiguous behavior is deeply compelling and makes her easy to love even when she\'s at her most flawed. Snow\'s performance anchors a story that could otherwise get lost in the chaos . 1 \'Murdaugh: Death in the Family\' (2025) Brittany Snow holding a phone out to someone on a beach in Murdaugh: Death in the Family. Image via Hulu Murdaugh: Death in the Family chronicles the shocking unraveling of the Murdaugh legal dynasty in South Carolina. The series follows Alex Murdaugh ( Jason Clarke ), a powerful attorney, and his wife Maggie ( Patricia Arquette ), as their gilded life unravels after their son Paul ( Johnny Berchtold ) is involved in a fatal boating accident. But the tragedy deepens when, two years later, Maggie and Paul are found shot dead on the family property. Snow plays Mandy Matney , a podcaster and blogger who investigated the case. Snow\'s role in Murdaugh: Death in the Family is a dramatic departure from many of her previous light-hearted roles. Because the story is based on real events, Snow\'s performance had to feel authentic. She succeeds in leaning into the gravity of this character, who\'s based on the woman who worked tirelessly to bring the truth to light . This is one of her most important projects since it\'s one of her most mature and layered performances to date. Released on November 13, The Beast in Me cast is led by Claire Danes as Aggie Wiggs, a celebrated author mourning the loss of her young son, who develops an obsession with her new next-door neighbor, Nile Jarvis (Matthew Rhys). Snow stars as Nina Jarvis, Nile\'s devoted second wife, whom he married following the mysterious disappearance of his first wife, Madison. Though it has since dropped to 83% on Rotten Tomatoes, The Beast in Me premiered to a rare 100% score . This beats The Hunting Wives , which sits at 76%, but the latter thriller is far superior. Thriller Fans Will Love The Sordid Secrets Of The Hunting Wives\' Main Characters Margot and Sophie looking excited while in the forest in The Hunting Wives Lionsgate/Netflix / Courtesy Everett Collection When we first meet Brittany Snow\'s Sophie O\'Neil in The Hunting Wives , we know she has secrets to hide. A Boston transplant, Sophie arrives at her new home in East Texas as a total fish out of water, having moved with her family for her husband Graham\'s (Evan Jonigkeit) job. She feels even more out of place at an NRA fundraising party hosted by Graham\'s boss, Jed Banks (Dermot Mulroney). However, Jed\'s wife, Margo (Malin Akerman), instantly takes a liking to Sophie and invites her to a girls\' night with her clique, the titular Hunting Wives. From there, Sophie is seduced by Margo\'s gun-toting, hard-drinking world, and much like us, Margo is desperate to know what\'s going on behind Sophie\'s skittish facade. But this doesn\'t even get to the heart of The Hunting Wives \' main storyline, which is the murder of local high school cheerleader Abby (Madison Wolfe). As Sophie is pulled into the investigation, more secrets are revealed, including the truth behind another local girl\'s disappearance, and affairs, affairs, affairs. No twist is boring, and each storyline is more sordid than the last without ever being exploitative. The Hunting Wives is an unapologetically vulgar show , and the show is just as fun as it is gripping, never taking itself too seriously. This sets it apart from more straitlaced thrillers like The Beast in Me , which is still worth watching, though it\'s not nearly as refreshing as The Hunting Wives . Brittany Snow Is Even Better In The Hunting Wives Than In The Beast In Me Sophie looks upset in The Hunting Wives There\'s no doubt about it — 2025 is definitely Brittany Snow\'s year. Having previously been pigeonholed as a teen genre actress thanks to her roles in Hairspray and the Pitch Perfect films, Snow has successfully made the leap to more grown-up fare with the incredibly not-safe-for-kids The Hunting Wives and The Beast in Me . Snow is terrific in both Netflix thriller series , and on the surface, her characters are quite similar, as both are well-off women married to controlling husbands. But more importantly, Sophie and Nina are both full of surprises. The difference is that, as the main character in The Hunting Wives , Snow has more room to play. We both get to know and care for Sophie deeply, while she still remains a complete mystery to us. As we inch closer to solving it, every revelation — from how she met her husband to her ability to kill — is a shock, but one we would have seen coming. In The Beast in Me , Nina has secrets of her own, but as she\'s a supporting character more defined by her relationship to her husband, the audience is kept at somewhat of an arm\'s length, and we don\'t really get to delve into her psyche the way we do Sophie\'s. The Hunting Wives will start filming season 2 later this month, and Brittany Snow promises it will be " crazier " than season 1. Whether we\'re seeing her as a nervous wife and mother, an eager-to-fit-in Hunting Wife, a prime murder suspect, or an unhinged woman having an absolute meltdown in a motel, Sophie O\'Neil is without a doubt the greatest role of Brittany Snow\'s career, making The Hunting Wives the superior Netflix thriller. By Adam Rathe Published: Nov 16, 2025 Courtesy of Netflix Brittany Snow seems to have a type: dangerous rich people. This year, the actress has starred in the hit series The Hunting Wives as a newcomer to an East Texas town where a group of well-heeled women lure her into a dangerous, debauched circle, and in Murdaugh: Death in the Family , as the journalist Mandy Matney, who investigated the murders that tore apart a South Caroline dynasty . Now, she’s playing a leading role in The Beast in Me , a gripping new series about a billionaire real-estate developer who might have had something to do with his wife’ mysterious disappearance—and who moves in next door to a writer desperate to find out. “It wasn\'t strategic at all,” Snow tells T&C . “Maybe I give off a type of energy because I\'m a type of person who can play a wide-eyed deer in headlights, but I find it very gratifying that I get to play someone in whom the audience can see themselves. It’s very satisfying that I get to be the audience in a lot of ways.” On Beast , Snow’s Nina does just that. She’s the second wife of the Nile Jarvis ( Matthew Rhys ), the Robert Durst-esque developer whose previous spouse seemingly disappeared, and while it’s Nile’s relationship with author-next-door Aggie Wiggs ( Claire Danes ) that drives much of the drama, Nina’s the one the audience looks to for clues about what Nile might or might not have done. And—spoiler alert—she’s the one who eventually delivers his comeuppance. This year, Brittany Snow has starred in series including The Hunting Wives and Murdaugh: Death in the Family . Lauren Withrow In the new series The Beast in Me , she plays Nina Jarvis, the wife of a billionaire suspected of offing her predecessor. Lauren Withrow “I was jumping to audition for it,” Snow says. “There were only two scripts that I got to read, but I just leapt at the opportunity because I had full faith in the people that were involved.” Also, because the opportunity to play the various layers of Nina was too tempting to pass up. “From the very beginning, we had to make the decision: does Nina truly not know; does she believe her husband; does she think that he\'s being genuine in the disappearance; is she complicit,” Snow says. “Just like a lot of women in these cases, when there\'s a man who\'s been suspected of murder, for survival and to be able to sleep at night, she makes the decision to not question anything. Nina is definitely the archetype for that of a woman who does believe the lie.” That is, until she doesn’t. The series gives Snow the chance to play her own game of cat and mouse: What does her character believe, how much does she want her husband to know, and what is she willing to do to continue being Mrs. Nile Jarvis. It’s a simmering situation that comes to a head in the series’ final episode and gives Snow some of the season’s most compelling scenes. Chris Saunders Brittany Snow and Matthew Rhys in The Beast in Me , streaming now on Netflix. “It was fun and challenging to play the levels and that duality,” Snow says. “Is she in on it? What is she using to her advantage? And then inevitably in the final scenes, knowing Nile\'s mannerisms and character so well, she\'s able to manipulate him for the first time.” Even filming those scenes required Snow to think of herself as something of a warrior. “She has to bait him, and she has to lure him,” she says. “There was a point when I asked Antonio [Campos, the finale’s director] if I could stand up because I order to get him to a primal place, she has to be a sparring partner, and she\'s learned that he responds well to someone being an adversary who compliments him in such a frightening way.” It wasn’t a given that the series would end up finding a hero in Nina. The series’ scripts were being written as it filmed, and Snow says, “we had no idea what the arc was going to be.” Through conversations with writers and producers, though, she lent her own take. “I did have a conversation with Daniel Pearle, our main writer and producer,” she says. “We were in my trailer, this was around episode five, and I said to him, ‘I have been underestimated and undermined a lot in my life, and I feel very connected to Nina in that way. There\'s something more to her that I think I would love to be able to show.’ I didn\'t know what would come from that conversation, and I don\'t know what motivated them to do this, but they made that twist because I think they respected the fact that Nina had also been undermined and underestimated. How interesting would it be if the person you don\'t see coming is the one who brings about the downfall?” “How interesting would it be if the person you don\'t see coming is the one who brings about the downfall?” Snow’s dedication to figuring out her character is no secret to her colleagues, or to the people who she’s played. The real Mandy Matney, the journalist who covered the Murdaugh case, says, “She cares so much and is so emotionally involved in the projects that she does, she really wants to make the people around her proud of her work. She kept being like, ‘I hope I\'m making you proud,’ and I was like, ‘This is the most amazing thing in the universe; I can\'t believe that you\'re here right now doing this and playing me.’” Erin Lee Carr, a creator and producer of the series, adds, “it\'s really difficult to play a journalist in a TV show, when you\'re doggedly pursuing the truth, but you\'re potentially not seeing the things for which you have blinders. It was such a complicated story and Brittany was able to manage that really effectively—we needed to an actress of her caliber to do it.” Three high-profile brushes with death and disaster, however, might not have been enough for Snow. “I go into filming season two of The Hunting Wives in two weeks,” she says. But then it might be time for something lighter. “After that, I hope I do a comedy,” she says. “No corpses, no murder.” Adam Rathe Deputy Features Director Adam Rathe is Town & Country\'s Deputy Features Director, covering film, theater, books, travel, art, philanthropy, and a range of other subjects. She considers herself a television nerd, diehard romance/sci-fi/fantasy reader, and nascent horror lover. Her fondness of books is only eclipsed by the towering TBR that her shelves can\'t possibly contain. She is the author of A REGENCY GUIDE TO MODERN LIFE: 1800s ADVICE ON 21ST CENTURY LOVE, FRIENDS, FUN AND MORE , published through DK Books (an imprint of Penguin Random House) and currently available wherever books are sold. While one of the biggest storylines in Murdaugh: Death in the Family revolves around the titular family, the Hulu true crime series also makes a point to spotlight the efforts of the journalist who originally followed the Murdaughs in real time. Long before the deaths of Maggie ( Patricia Arquette ) and Paul Murdaugh ( Johnny Berchtold ), for which family patriarch Alex Murdaugh ( Jason Clarke ) would ultimately be convicted and sentenced to prison , a devastating boat crash snowballs into a much broader investigation about the Murdaughs and the secrets they might be hiding. Co-created by Michael D. Fuller and Erin Lee Carr , Murdaugh: Death in the Family is largely inspired by the efforts of the Murdaugh Murders Podcast from Mandy Matney . Ahead of the show\'s premiere, Collider had the opportunity to speak with several people behind Murdaugh: Death in the Family , including Matney and Brittany Snow , who plays the series\' version of the real-life journalist. Over the course of the interview, which you can watch above or read below, Snow admits that her true crime obsession paid off long before she was cast in the series, while the two reflect on their early collaboration and also explain why it wouldn\'t have really made sense to give Mandy a big confrontation scene with Alex Murdaugh in the finale. COLLIDER: There\'s so much to talk about pertaining to this show, but a good place to start is going all the way back to the beginning, and I feel like that starts with you, Mandy, because this show is inspired by the work that you did on the podcast, following this case in real time and breaking a lot of the information. How early did you become involved with the project, and how closely did you end up working with Michael [D. Fuller] and Erin [Lee Carr] in shaping it? MANDY MATNEY: I guess my work on this project began in February 2019, when I first found out about the boat crash, and as a reporter, I just dug in and couldn\'t stop. Then everything went, obviously, haywire in 2021, and at that point, I had years of research and investigative journalism built up about the Murdaugh family that I had to make a podcast and put all of that out there. Then, a few months after we first launched the podcast, I was connected with Erin Lee Carr, and originally, I was connected with her for a documentary. We were thinking of doing a documentary because, of course, she\'s the queen of documentaries, and I was so excited because I had been a huge fan of hers for the longest time. I\'ve never been more nervous for an interview, I don\'t think, than when I Zoomed with Erin Lee Carr, because I was like, “Oh my gosh, you\'re so cool!” And then from there, she kind of started developing the idea of making it a scripted series and working with Michael D. Fuller, who\'s a South Carolina native and really understood the story and understood the corruption surrounding the story. Both of them, we really connected with them on the fact that they were victim-forward and what they wanted to do with the story, and I like the questions that they asked. Then from there, we just let them make a majority of the creative decisions, and I\'m so proud of them. They did an amazing job. It sounds like this has been a long-gestating series. Was there any new information that ended up coming out while this was taking shape, where you had to go back and tweak some things, or add things that weren\'t initially planned for? MATNEY: That\'s a good question. By the time we were officially greenlit and the series was going, which was about a year ago, most of the facts of the story were already out there. Still, like today, one of Alex\'s accomplices is in state court. There are things like that that are still ongoing, but the main events that we focused on in the show happened years ago . So, not a lot changed. Brittany, coming into this, how much awareness did you have of the case, and did you find yourself looking into it more once you knew you were playing Mandy, who very doggedly was investigating this in real time? BRITTANY SNOW: Luckily for me, I am such a big true crime person. It\'s my favorite thing to dig into. And a lot of the time, I think to myself, “Wow, I\'m listening to a lot of true crime podcasts. I hope this is not a waste of time.” And in this instance, for the first time ever, my hours and hours and hours of listening to Mandy\'s podcast years ago were not a waste of time . I actually was doing research before I even knew I was doing research, so I was very well aware of the case and of Mandy. I was going into my meeting with Erin Lee Carr and Michael D. Fuller with so much excitement and knowledge, because I had theories and I had reasons, and so it was really exciting to me to get to learn even more and do even more research once I got the role. Brittany Snow in Murdaugh: Death in the Family Episode 7 Image via Hulu Did the two of you connect early on, Mandy, so you could give her any insight? MATNEY: We did that right away! SNOW: Immediately. MATNEY: I was a big fan of hers and literally squealed when I found out that there was a possibility of Brittany Snow playing me, and then you followed me on Instagram, and I was like, “Oh my God! This is the best day ever!” I really didn\'t believe Erin when she said that you were a fan of the podcast . Some people say that sometimes, and they\'re not, and you can tell when you talk to them. So, we chatted on Instagram and met up in Atlanta a few weeks later. SNOW: I called you. MATNEY: Oh yeah! You called me. I need to talk to Mandy Matney.” So that\'s where my priorities were. And we just hit it off. MATNEY: I could tell immediately that she knew the story. She wasn\'t one of those that’s, like, “Oh, I like your podcast,” and then, like, mispronounces things. You knew all of the people, all of the players, everything. SNOW: And I had questions. MATNEY: And details. You remembered everything. It was super impressive. This is sort of a two-pronged Hunting Wives question about whether you\'ve seen the SNL sketch already — I\'m assuming it was probably sent to you countless times over — and if there\'s anything that you can tease about where Season 2 is at in development. SNOW: So I got wind of the SNL sketch like an hour before it aired, and so I raced home and watched it live. That was a crazy moment. It was so great. And Chloe [Fineman] did me perfectly. We were all very, very excited. And then Season 2, we\'re starting to film in a couple of weeks. Brittany Snow Explains Why She Didn\'t Have More Scenes With Her \'Murdaugh: Death in the Family\' Castmates "That\'s not the power that Mandy had..." Brittany Snow in the Murdaugh: Death in the Family finale Image via Hulu In watching this, sometimes it feels like you\'re siloed off from the rest of the cast, and there were times where I was hoping to see you get a little bit more of a chance to really bounce off some of the central figures, but also, you want to keep this as accurate and true to life as possible. Brittany, did you ever find yourself having moments where you wished you had more of those opportunities to face off with Jason [Clarke] or Patricia [Arquette], or get more of those scenes, or were you content with how the storyline ended up playing out through the season? SNOW: It was so important for this to be accurate, and I think a lot of times in movies and TV shows, it\'s good TV and not necessarily accurate for the reporter to have a big scene and throw elbows with the people . But that\'s not the power that Mandy had, like through force. It was through her intellect, and it was through her figuring out what really happened. So, I really liked that it was sort of seen like it was behind the scenes that she was siloed off, but really, that\'s where she did the most work, and that\'s what you see today in how it\'s portrayed. So, I appreciated the accuracy of that. MATNEY: Agreed. That\'s reflective of reality. We\'ve talked about this: a lot of times, Hollywood does not get the journalist’s storyline correct . Like you said, a scene with me and Alex would just be stupid and unnecessary. I was busy exposing him to millions of people; if I was going to yell at him, that wouldn\'t have helped anything at the time. SNOW: And a lot of the drama that you went through that was seen and a little bit alluded to in the show is that she was dealing, also, with the fact of being ostracized by her bosses and people not taking her seriously on this job and where this story was going to lead. All of those intricacies woven into the story, I think, are just as important, because it really showed how much adversity she went through in order to get this story through and over the line . From her early days in teen dramas to her breakout roles in musical comedies and emotionally resonant movies and TV series, she has consistently shown that she can slip into any character with ease . Whether she\'s delivering sharp comedic timing, heartfelt vulnerability, or powerhouse vocals, Snow brings a warmth and relatability that has made audiences root for her for more than two decades. As an artist, Snow has chosen projects that span genres including rom-coms, thrillers, ensemble musicals, and dramas. This range has made it difficult for fans to pick just one definitive "best" performance, because she shines in so many different ways. Still, a handful of movies and TV shows stand out as milestones in her career, shaping her identity as one of Hollywood\'s most consistently compelling talents. The best Brittany Snow projects highlight her ability to leave a lasting impression whether in a leading role or as part of a larger ensemble . 10 \'Crazy Ex Girlfriend\' (2015–2019) A closeup of Brittany Snow looking at the camera and talking in Crazy Ex Girlfriend. Image via The CW Crazy Ex-Girlfriend is a musical comedy-drama that follows Rebecca Bunch ( Rachel Bloom ), a high-powered but unhappy New York lawyer who impulsively moves to West Covina, California, after a chance encounter with her childhood crush, Josh Chan ( Vincent Rodriguez III ). What begins as a romantic quest quickly becomes a deeper exploration of mental health, identity, and the pursuit of happiness . Snow plays Josh\'s girlfriend Anna Hicks, who is introduced in the series\' second season. While this is a recurring role, Snow\'s character in Crazy Ex-Girlfriend immediately makes an impact because she subverts the expectations of a "mean girl". Snow brings a perfect balance of over-the-top arrogance and subtle vulnerability to a character who is a star from the background. Crazy Ex-Girlfriend is also a musical comedy, and Snow’s performance showcased her vocal chops . Songs like "Research Me Obsessively" allowed her to combine humor, musicality, and storytelling in a way that few of her previous roles demanded. 9 \'The Beast in Me\' (2025–) Brittany Snow in a tan blazer staring ahead in The Beast in Me. Image via Netflix The Beast in Me is a psychological thriller series that introduces Aggie Wiggs ( Claire Danes ), a successful author who’s been paralyzed by grief after the death of her young son. After finding herself unable to write, her life takes a dark turn when Nile Jarvis ( Matthew Rhys ), a wealthy real estate heir with a secretive past, moves in next door. As Aggie becomes obsessed with his story, she embarks on a dangerous game of cat-and-mouse . Snow plays Nina Jarvis, Nile\'s second wife. Brittany Snow stands out in The Beast in Me because she\'s able to subvert the expectations of what many would expect of a "wife" character. This is a darker, more dramatic role than many of the others she\'s known for. Although Nina isn\'t a central character in this story, Snow makes her stand out and makes it clear that she\'s never to be underestimated . In particular, Snow portrays her as someone with something to hide and her own motivations that make her a potential threat to those around her. 8 \'Someone Great\' (2019) Blair (Brittany Snow) asking for party drugs on the way to Neon Classic in Someone Great. Image via Netflix Someone Great is a romantic comedy that follows Jenny ( Gina Rodriguez ), a music journalist in New York City who lands her dream job in San Francisco, only to be heartbroken when her boyfriend of nine years, Nate ( LaKeith Stanfield ), breaks up with her. Reeling from the breakup, Jenny leans on her two best friends, Erin ( DeWanda Wise ) and Blair ( Brittany Snow ), to take her on one last wild day in the city . They skip work, party, chase concert tickets, and confront big life decisions that they\'ve been putting off. Someone Great gives Snow a chance to showcase how well she\'s able to shine in a strong ensemble. This movie isn’t just a fairy-tale rom‑com. Instead, it tackles real heartbreak, life transitions, and self-discovery. Snow is able to tap into Blair\'s humanity and highlight the fact that she\'s trying to navigate these tough issues with nuance and grace . Blair is exactly the type of character that Snow is so perfectly suited to play, since she\'s sweet, funny, and just trying to do the best she can. 7 \'American Dreams\' (2002–2005) Brittany Snow and the cast of American Dreams standing together in front of their home. Image via NBC American Dreams is a period drama set in 1960s Philadelphia. The series introduces the Pryor family, who do their best to navigate the seismic cultural shifts of the era. The show specifically follows Meg Pryor (Snow), a teenage girl whose dream is to dance on American Bandstand , and her journey growing up amid political unrest, civil rights struggles, and the Vietnam War . Alongside her, her brothers, parents, and friends deal with changing gender roles, racism, war, and social upheaval. American Dreams is one of Snow\'s most notable series since it was one of her first major TV roles . She convincingly captures the plight of a teenage girl growing up in the 1960s in America navigating ambition, family challenges, and social change. Meg evolves from a dream-filled teen into a young woman confronting real-world issues like prejudice, war, and personal responsibility, allowing Snow to play both lighthearted and deeply emotional scenes. This is an early look at Snow\'s talents and how she was able to shine from the earliest days of her career. 6 \'Pitch Perfect\' (2012) Pitch Perfect is a musical comedy that introduces Beca ( Anna Kendrick ), a college freshman with a passion for music, who reluctantly joins the Barden University a cappella group, the Bellas . The all-female group, mocked for their outdated style and internal conflicts, struggles to regain their former glory in the competitive world of collegiate a cappella. The Bellas are co-led by Chloe Beale (Snow), who recognizes that the group needs Beca\'s talent if they want a chance of succeeding. Pitch Perfect is one of Snow\'s best movies because it allowed her to showcase a mix of talents that play to her strengths, including acting, singing, and comedic timing, all in a single role. Snow\'s charm and stage presence help balance the movie\'s musical performances with its comedic and emotional moments . Additionally, Pitch Perfect \'s popularity and cult status gave her career a big boost, making it one of her most memorable and defining roles. 5 \'Hairspray\' (2007) Zac Efron and Brittany Snow in \'Hairspray\' Image via New Line Cinema Hairspray is a musical comedy set in 1960s Baltimore that follows Tracy Turnblad ( Nikki Blonsky ), a spirited and plus-sized teenager with big dreams of dancing on a local TV dance show. When she lands a spot on the program, Tracy uses her newfound fame to challenge the show\'s racial segregation and fight for integration. Snow plays Amber Von Tussle, the lead female dancer on "The Corny Collins Show" who feels threatened by Tracy\'s talent . Hairspray stands out as one of Snow\'s best movies because it gives her a chance to be a compelling villain to root against . More than being a bratty teenager, she represents the worst parts of American society with her attitude of entitlement and refusal to consider anyone other than herself. Snow fully leans into the camp and charisma needed for the role, making Amber both entertaining and memorable rather than a one-note villain. 4 \'John Tucker Must Die\' (2006) Brittany Snow as Kate looking at someone and smiling in John Tucker Must Die. Image via 20th Century Studios John Tucker Must Die is a teen comedy about three popular high-school girls who discover they\'ve all been secretly dating the same charming but manipulative basketball star, John Tucker ( Jesse Metcalfe ). Furious, they recruit a shy new girl, Kate (Snow), to help them take him down by transforming her into his dream girl and then publicly breaking his heart . Their revenge plans escalate and include everything ranging from embarrassing pranks to emotional sabotage. John Tucker Must Die is one of Brittany Snow\'s best movies because it showcases her strengths as a comedic and relatable leading actress . Snow brings sincerity, great timing, and a sweet vulnerability to this role, which is essential to the story\'s over-the-top antics. John Tucker Must Die gives her space to be funny, charming, and emotionally compelling all at once, and her performance helps elevate the ensemble that makes the movie so enjoyable. 3 \'X\' (2022) Brittany Snow in a red jumpsuit rests by a gas pump with a cameraman nearby in X. Image via A24 X is a slasher-horror movie set in 1979 that follows a small group of aspiring filmmakers who rent a rural Texas farmhouse to secretly shoot an adult film. The elderly owners, Pearl ( Mia Goth ) and Howard ( Stephen Ure ), seem odd but harmless at first, until Pearl becomes fixated on the youth and sexuality of the visitors, triggering a violent, nightmarish killing spree . Snow plays Bobby-Lynne, a burlesque dancer who is trying her best to build a career. X is one of Brittany Snow\'s best movies because it lets her step outside the wholesome or comedic roles she\'s most associated with and delivers a bold, memorable performance in a gritty horror setting. As Bobby-Lynne, she brings charisma, humor, and surprising emotional depth to a character who could\'ve been forgettable . Snow balances confidence and vulnerability in a way that makes Bobby-Lynne stand out within the ensemble and her presence adds levity and heart to a movie that\'s otherwise dark and intense. 2 \'The Hunting Wives\' (2025–) Malin Akerman as Margo teaches Brittany Snow as Sophie to fire a gun in the pilot of The Hunting Wives. Image via Netflix The Hunting Wives follows Sophie O\'Neill (Snow), a woman who leaves behind her busy Chicago life for what she hopes will be a quieter, more fulfilling existence in the small town of Mapleton, Texas. There she becomes entangled with a seductive, privileged social circle led by the magnetic and manipulative Margot Banks ( Malin Akerman ). The group\'s glamorous façade hides darker obsessions. The Hunting Wives follows these women as they party, host secret shooting outings, and engage in increasingly reckless behavior. The Hunting Wives is one of Brittany Snow\'s standout projects, not just because of her performance, but because of the way the series combines psychological suspense with social drama . Sophie\'s transformation from outsider to someone entangled in dark, morally ambiguous behavior is deeply compelling and makes her easy to love even when she\'s at her most flawed. Snow\'s performance anchors a story that could otherwise get lost in the chaos . 1 \'Murdaugh: Death in the Family\' (2025) Brittany Snow holding a phone out to someone on a beach in Murdaugh: Death in the Family. Image via Hulu Murdaugh: Death in the Family chronicles the shocking unraveling of the Murdaugh legal dynasty in South Carolina. The series follows Alex Murdaugh ( Jason Clarke ), a powerful attorney, and his wife Maggie ( Patricia Arquette ), as their gilded life unravels after their son Paul ( Johnny Berchtold ) is involved in a fatal boating accident. But the tragedy deepens when, two years later, Maggie and Paul are found shot dead on the family property. Snow plays Mandy Matney , a podcaster and blogger who investigated the case. Snow\'s role in Murdaugh: Death in the Family is a dramatic departure from many of her previous light-hearted roles. Because the story is based on real events, Snow\'s performance had to feel authentic. She succeeds in leaning into the gravity of this character, who\'s based on the woman who worked tirelessly to bring the truth to light . This is one of her most important projects since it\'s one of her most mature and layered performances to date. Released on November 13, The Beast in Me cast is led by Claire Danes as Aggie Wiggs, a celebrated author mourning the loss of her young son, who develops an obsession with her new next-door neighbor, Nile Jarvis (Matthew Rhys). Snow stars as Nina Jarvis, Nile\'s devoted second wife, whom he married following the mysterious disappearance of his first wife, Madison. Though it has since dropped to 83% on Rotten Tomatoes, The Beast in Me premiered to a rare 100% score . This beats The Hunting Wives , which sits at 76%, but the latter thriller is far superior. Thriller Fans Will Love The Sordid Secrets Of The Hunting Wives\' Main Characters Margot and Sophie looking excited while in the forest in The Hunting Wives Lionsgate/Netflix / Courtesy Everett Collection When we first meet Brittany Snow\'s Sophie O\'Neil in The Hunting Wives , we know she has secrets to hide. A Boston transplant, Sophie arrives at her new home in East Texas as a total fish out of water, having moved with her family for her husband Graham\'s (Evan Jonigkeit) job. She feels even more out of place at an NRA fundraising party hosted by Graham\'s boss, Jed Banks (Dermot Mulroney). However, Jed\'s wife, Margo (Malin Akerman), instantly takes a liking to Sophie and invites her to a girls\' night with her clique, the titular Hunting Wives. From there, Sophie is seduced by Margo\'s gun-toting, hard-drinking world, and much like us, Margo is desperate to know what\'s going on behind Sophie\'s skittish facade. But this doesn\'t even get to the heart of The Hunting Wives \' main storyline, which is the murder of local high school cheerleader Abby (Madison Wolfe). As Sophie is pulled into the investigation, more secrets are revealed, including the truth behind another local girl\'s disappearance, and affairs, affairs, affairs. No twist is boring, and each storyline is more sordid than the last without ever being exploitative. The Hunting Wives is an unapologetically vulgar show , and the show is just as fun as it is gripping, never taking itself too seriously. This sets it apart from more straitlaced thrillers like The Beast in Me , which is still worth watching, though it\'s not nearly as refreshing as The Hunting Wives . Brittany Snow Is Even Better In The Hunting Wives Than In The Beast In Me Sophie looks upset in The Hunting Wives There\'s no doubt about it — 2025 is definitely Brittany Snow\'s year. Having previously been pigeonholed as a teen genre actress thanks to her roles in Hairspray and the Pitch Perfect films, Snow has successfully made the leap to more grown-up fare with the incredibly not-safe-for-kids The Hunting Wives and The Beast in Me . Snow is terrific in both Netflix thriller series , and on the surface, her characters are quite similar, as both are well-off women married to controlling husbands. But more importantly, Sophie and Nina are both full of surprises. The difference is that, as the main character in The Hunting Wives , Snow has more room to play. We both get to know and care for Sophie deeply, while she still remains a complete mystery to us. As we inch closer to solving it, every revelation — from how she met her husband to her ability to kill — is a shock, but one we would have seen coming. In The Beast in Me , Nina has secrets of her own, but as she\'s a supporting character more defined by her relationship to her husband, the audience is kept at somewhat of an arm\'s length, and we don\'t really get to delve into her psyche the way we do Sophie\'s. The Hunting Wives will start filming season 2 later this month, and Brittany Snow promises it will be " crazier " than season 1. Whether we\'re seeing her as a nervous wife and mother, an eager-to-fit-in Hunting Wife, a prime murder suspect, or an unhinged woman having an absolute meltdown in a motel, Sophie O\'Neil is without a doubt the greatest role of Brittany Snow\'s career, making The Hunting Wives the superior Netflix thriller. By Adam Rathe Published: Nov 16, 2025 Courtesy of Netflix Brittany Snow seems to have a type: dangerous rich people. This year, the actress has starred in the hit series The Hunting Wives as a newcomer to an East Texas town where a group of well-heeled women lure her into a dangerous, debauched circle, and in Murdaugh: Death in the Family , as the journalist Mandy Matney, who investigated the murders that tore apart a South Caroline dynasty . Now, she’s playing a leading role in The Beast in Me , a gripping new series about a billionaire real-estate developer who might have had something to do with his wife’ mysterious disappearance—and who moves in next door to a writer desperate to find out. “It wasn\'t strategic at all,” Snow tells T&C . “Maybe I give off a type of energy because I\'m a type of person who can play a wide-eyed deer in headlights, but I find it very gratifying that I get to play someone in whom the audience can see themselves. It’s very satisfying that I get to be the audience in a lot of ways.” On Beast , Snow’s Nina does just that. She’s the second wife of the Nile Jarvis ( Matthew Rhys ), the Robert Durst-esque developer whose previous spouse seemingly disappeared, and while it’s Nile’s relationship with author-next-door Aggie Wiggs ( Claire Danes ) that drives much of the drama, Nina’s the one the audience looks to for clues about what Nile might or might not have done. And—spoiler alert—she’s the one who eventually delivers his comeuppance. This year, Brittany Snow has starred in series including The Hunting Wives and Murdaugh: Death in the Family . Lauren Withrow In the new series The Beast in Me , she plays Nina Jarvis, the wife of a billionaire suspected of offing her predecessor. Lauren Withrow “I was jumping to audition for it,” Snow says. “There were only two scripts that I got to read, but I just leapt at the opportunity because I had full faith in the people that were involved.” Also, because the opportunity to play the various layers of Nina was too tempting to pass up. “From the very beginning, we had to make the decision: does Nina truly not know; does she believe her husband; does she think that he\'s being genuine in the disappearance; is she complicit,” Snow says. “Just like a lot of women in these cases, when there\'s a man who\'s been suspected of murder, for survival and to be able to sleep at night, she makes the decision to not question anything. Nina is definitely the archetype for that of a woman who does believe the lie.” That is, until she doesn’t. The series gives Snow the chance to play her own game of cat and mouse: What does her character believe, how much does she want her husband to know, and what is she willing to do to continue being Mrs. Nile Jarvis. It’s a simmering situation that comes to a head in the series’ final episode and gives Snow some of the season’s most compelling scenes. Chris Saunders Brittany Snow and Matthew Rhys in The Beast in Me , streaming now on Netflix. “It was fun and challenging to play the levels and that duality,” Snow says. “Is she in on it? What is she using to her advantage? And then inevitably in the final scenes, knowing Nile\'s mannerisms and character so well, she\'s able to manipulate him for the first time.” Even filming those scenes required Snow to think of herself as something of a warrior. “She has to bait him, and she has to lure him,” she says. “There was a point when I asked Antonio [Campos, the finale’s director] if I could stand up because I order to get him to a primal place, she has to be a sparring partner, and she\'s learned that he responds well to someone being an adversary who compliments him in such a frightening way.” It wasn’t a given that the series would end up finding a hero in Nina. The series’ scripts were being written as it filmed, and Snow says, “we had no idea what the arc was going to be.” Through conversations with writers and producers, though, she lent her own take. “I did have a conversation with Daniel Pearle, our main writer and producer,” she says. “We were in my trailer, this was around episode five, and I said to him, ‘I have been underestimated and undermined a lot in my life, and I feel very connected to Nina in that way. There\'s something more to her that I think I would love to be able to show.’ I didn\'t know what would come from that conversation, and I don\'t know what motivated them to do this, but they made that twist because I think they respected the fact that Nina had also been undermined and underestimated. How interesting would it be if the person you don\'t see coming is the one who brings about the downfall?” “How interesting would it be if the person you don\'t see coming is the one who brings about the downfall?” Snow’s dedication to figuring out her character is no secret to her colleagues, or to the people who she’s played. The real Mandy Matney, the journalist who covered the Murdaugh case, says, “She cares so much and is so emotionally involved in the projects that she does, she really wants to make the people around her proud of her work. She kept being like, ‘I hope I\'m making you proud,’ and I was like, ‘This is the most amazing thing in the universe; I can\'t believe that you\'re here right now doing this and playing me.’” Erin Lee Carr, a creator and producer of the series, adds, “it\'s really difficult to play a journalist in a TV show, when you\'re doggedly pursuing the truth, but you\'re potentially not seeing the things for which you have blinders. It was such a complicated story and Brittany was able to manage that really effectively—we needed to an actress of her caliber to do it.” Three high-profile brushes with death and disaster, however, might not have been enough for Snow. “I go into filming season two of The Hunting Wives in two weeks,” she says. But then it might be time for something lighter. “After that, I hope I do a comedy,” she says. “No corpses, no murder.” Adam Rathe Deputy Features Director Adam Rathe is Town & Country\'s Deputy Features Director, covering film, theater, books, travel, art, philanthropy, and a range of other subjects. She considers herself a television nerd, diehard romance/sci-fi/fantasy reader, and nascent horror lover. Her fondness of books is only eclipsed by the towering TBR that her shelves can\'t possibly contain. She is the author of A REGENCY GUIDE TO MODERN LIFE: 1800s ADVICE ON 21ST CENTURY LOVE, FRIENDS, FUN AND MORE , published through DK Books (an imprint of Penguin Random House) and currently available wherever books are sold.
