Beauty, and More Here’s a look at some steal-worthy ideas we spotted in November 2025. Claire Hoffman , Senior Contributing Editor November 25, 2025 14 Min Read e.l.f. Beauty’s “Give an e.l.f.” pop-up raised $50,000 for nonprofits chosen by the community. Scroll down for more. Photo: Tory Stolper Photography Once a month, BizBash brings you even more inspiration for your own gatherings with our "Cool Event Ideas of the Month" column, where we round up some of the creative ideas we haven\'t had the chance to cover yet. Our November 2025 roundup includes L.L.Bean\'s cozy ode to flannel, e.l.f. Beauty\'s custom donation kiosk, Uber Eats Canada’s data-driven hockey activation, and Absolut\'s eye-catching bar at the Wicked: For Good premiere. Scroll on to see these and more from brands like Kate Spade, Hello Sunshine, and Disney+. L.L.Bean NYC Residency From Oct. 18 through Nov. 30, L.L.Bean has brought its six-week residency to New York City, inviting guests into an immersive space centered on the comfort and nostalgia of flannel. Open Wednesday through Sunday each week, the residency encourages visitors to explore, personalize, and discover timeless classics, with weekly expansions into sweaters, outerwear, holiday essentials, and cold-weather accessories. Photo: Sara Kerens Programming throughout the residency has included free embroidery by Abbode, a whimsical Halloween lineup with movie screenings and themed mocktails, exclusive Harris Tweed pieces, a curated vintage selection from Wooden Sleepers, and holiday gift-giving moments featuring refreshments and a charm bar. The rotating assortment and seasonal touchpoints offers guests new discoveries with each visit. Photo: Sara Karens The residency was produced by Factory360 . Photo: Sarah Kerens Hello Sunshine’s Sunniefest On Nov. 15 at Pegasus Park in Dallas, Hello Sunshine hosted its inaugural Sunniefest, an immersive festival co-created with Gen Z girls to spark connection, creativity, and self-expression. Produced by Mirrored Media , the full-day program featured conversations with next-gen talent—including Jacey Adler, Marley Dias, Kiernan Shipka, Neha Shukla, and others—alongside hands-on workshops, bespoke activations, and branded pop-ups designed to inspire and empower attendees. Photo: Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images for Hello Sunshine Cozy seating complemented a lineup of workshops led by creators, advocates, and Hello Sunshine Collective members, plus interactive offerings from partners like Coach, Victoria’s Secret PINK, and e.l.f. Beauty. The festival also marked the launch of Sunnie Reads, a new Gen Z–driven book club developed in partnership with Coach. Photo: Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images for Hello Sunshine The festival’s STEM Lab, presented by Lyda Hill Philanthropies’ IF/THEN initiative, invited attendees to dive into scent science, robotics, and hands-on experimentation with guidance from AAAS IF/THEN ambassadors Jenn Makins and Dr. Jennifer Stimpson. Nearby, Purdue University encouraged girls to explore future career paths through a photo-ready mural, postcard wall, and a session with AI expert and faculty member Kasie Roberson, PhD. Photo: Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images for Hello Sunshine e.l.f. Beauty\'s “Give an e.l.f.” Pop-Up On Oct. 28 in New York, e.l.f. Beauty hosted an all-day pop-up at Astor Place and Lafayette Street to mark the release of its fourth annual Impact Report and celebrate its “Give an e.l.f.” campaign. Nearly 1,000 community members stopped by to make their values count by selecting a cause at a custom donation kiosk—triggering a donation from e.l.f.—and redeeming their receipt at a gift bar for products. Photo: Tory Stolper Photography Across the activation, e.l.f. contributed $50,000 to six nonprofits chosen by the community: RISE, the It Gets Better Project, Look Good Feel Better, Best Friends Animal Society, and the Billie Jean King Foundation. The Bait Shoppe handled creative, production, and fabrication for the pop-up. Photo: Tory Stolper Photography Balloon Museum’s “Pop Air—Art Is Inflatable” Exhibition On Nov. 15 in Houston, the Balloon Museum opened "Pop Air—Art Is Inflatable," a large-scale exhibition created by Italy-based Lux Entertainment . Spanning more than 65,000 square feet, the showcase—which runs through April 2026—brings together luminous displays, interactive environments, and inflatable installations from 14 international artists, inviting visitors of all ages to explore the intersection of art, air, and play. Photo: Courtesy of Balloon Museum Featured works include Cyril Lancelin’s "Crazy Love for Polygons," Hyperstudio’s "Glowing Ballet," "10 Agosto," and "Hypercosmo," "Soft Hurricane" by Quiet Ensemble, ENESS’s "Spiritus Sonata," Karina Smigla-Bobinski’s "ADA," and Max Streicher’s "Silenius." The exhibition also incorporates digital experiences like Ultravioletto’s VR installation and Pepper’s Ghost’s ARIA infinity room, alongside participatory works from MOTOREFISICO (pictured), Pneuhaus & Bike Powered Events, Jimmy Kuehnle, Rub Kandy, and Filthy Luker. Photo: Courtesy of Balloon Museum Uber Eats Canada’s "Crave the Stats" Activation To celebrate hockey home openers in Toronto and Vancouver, Uber Eats Canada launched Crave the Stats, a data-driven activation that turned game-day food habits into part of the stat sheet. Outside Scotiabank Arena and Rogers Arena, the brand set up massive Uber Eats bags—20 feet tall in Toronto and 16 feet tall in Vancouver—inviting fans to engage with food-and-hockey trivia while spotlighting ordering trends from the 2024–2025 season. Photo: Courtesy of Uber Eats Canada Fans lined up for interactive challenges and on-the-spot prizes, including Uber Eats vouchers, game-night tickets, signed merch, and meet-and-greets with hockey legends Darcy Tucker and Chris Higgins. The builds drew thousands of participants across both markets and generated more than 2.3 million influencer impressions, surpassing category engagement benchmarks. Photo: Courtesy of Uber Eats Canada The campaign was created by T1 , with fabrication by MAWG and media by Touche! Photo: Courtesy of Uber Eats Canada Kate Spade New York x NYLON “Holiday Duo-ets” On Nov. 4 in Los Angeles, Kate Spade New York and NYLON transformed the Chateau Marmont Penthouse into a wintery, music-filled setting for “Holiday Duo-ets,” a celebration of togetherness and the spirit of gifting. Guests enjoyed festive cocktails, piano sing-alongs, and an immersive holiday environment anchored by a snow sculpture of the brand’s signature Duo bag. Photo: Nina Fernandez/BFA.com Inside, framed photos of guests at the event were used as tree ornaments. Brand ambassadors Ice Spice and Laufey led the evening, joined by Reign Judge, NYLON members, and attendees who included Kelsey Anderson, Rachael Kirkconnell, Baron Schoenvogel, Zoi Lerma, and more. The event was inspired by Kate Spade New York’s “Spark Something Beautiful” holiday campaign. Photo: Nina Fernandez/BFA.com TIRTIR’s “Radiant Pop-Up” On Nov. 14 in Los Angeles, global K-beauty brand TIRTIR debuted its immersive “Radiant Pop-Up” on Melrose Avenue. The installation marks a major moment for the brand—introducing a new logo, announcing global ambassador V, and bringing its “Your Shade, Our Standard” campaign to life through the experiential concept “V&You, Let’s Radiate.” A pre-opening event welcomed celebrities, influencers, and media. Photo: Courtesy of TIRTIR Inside the pop-up, guests could explore TIRTIR’s core complexion and skincare lineup, including the Mask Fit Red Cushion Foundation, Mask Fit AI Filter Cushion, Waterism Glow Tint, Milk Skin Toner, Matcha Skin Toner, and the new Banana BDRN. Interactive zones were designed to let visitors test textures, performance, and formulations firsthand while showcasing the brand’s updated aesthetic and identity. Photo: Courtesy of TIRTIR The pop-up ran through Nov. 23 and served as the starting point for additional experiential activations planned across major North American cities as the brand continues to grow its presence. Photo: Courtesy of TIRTIR The Owen’s Mixery at Warped Tour Orlando At Warped Tour Orlando, Owen’s Craft Mixers brought The Owen’s Mixery to life, marking the first in-person activation tied to MGK’s new role as the brand’s creative taste officer. Before his headlining set, MGK stopped by to pour mocktails and meet fans, drawing a crowd and highlighting the brand’s connection to music and fan culture. Photo: Courtesy of Owen’s Craft Mixers The Mixery aimed to reimagine the typical festival bar with custom cocktail and mocktail builds guided by an on-site mixologist, a window-service bar, and a playful “Owen the Mule” photo moment. The activation is part of Owen’s expanding partnership with Live Nation, spanning more than 100 venues and festivals nationwide. Photo: Courtesy of Owen’s Craft Mixers Absolut Activation at the Wicked: For Good Premiere Last week, 160over90 ’s experiential team supported Absolut at the NYC premiere of Wicked: For Good . As the film’s official partner, Absolut activated on the red carpet with a six-foot bar and back bar positioned along the press line, appearing prominently as cast members arrived and conducted interviews. Photo: Courtesy of 160over90 The setup showcased the limited-edition Absolut bottle in a pink-and-green sequin sleeve, and guests sampled themed cocktails including the Absolut x Ozmopolitan, Absolut x Thrillifying! Twist, and the Absolut & Kahlúa x Ozpresso Martini. Photo: Courtesy of 160over90 PatPat’s Holiday Movie Lounge On Nov. 12 in West Hollywood, families kicked off the season at PatPat’s Holiday Movie Lounge at E.P. & L.P.’s Melrose Rooftop Theatre. The event brought together families and celebrity guests—including Audrina Patridge, Chanel West Coast, Amber Stevens West, Anna Maria Perez de Tagle, Taylor Selfridge, Chelsea Tavares, Caroline D’Amore, Joey Tierney, and Danielle Ruiz—for a cozy evening of crafts, treats, and holiday fun hosted by the kids and family apparel brand. Photo: Stephanie Loren Photography Guests settled in beneath the stars for a rooftop screening of Disney’s Frozen , many wearing matching PatPat Disney sweaters and family pajamas to mark the start of the holidays. Photo: Stephanie Loren Photography Gravity One’s “First Round’s On Us” Activation Outside Adweek Brandweek in Atlanta, Gravity One —a new division of Gravity Global focused on breakthrough B2C work—staged a tongue-in-cheek guerrilla activation aimed directly at marketing decision-makers. A digital truck parked at the venue entrance flashed the message “IS YOUR BRAND WEAK?”, directing attendees to BrandWeak.com to enter for a chance to win a free first round of brand work, including strategy and creative. Photo: Courtesy of Gravity One Pro Padel League’s 2025 City’s Cup Finals Held Oct. 16-19 in Manhattan, the Pro Padel League’s 2025 City’s Cup Finals transformed the Hammerstein Ballroom into a full-scale padel arena for more than 5,000 fans. The four-day tournament featured matches with top-ranked players, culminating in the New York Atlantics taking home the season-long title. With Halloween and all things spooky officially come to an end, it’s that time of year for holiday films. From Hallmark to Lifetime, streaming services like Netflix and beyond, viewers can expect heartwarming stories with happy endings set against beautiful backdrops, along with delightful cooking shows. This guide will help you get into the holiday spirit. BET+ ”Christmas By Design” A famous handbag designer working on a special-edition holiday line for charity finds her newest designs stolen in a company data breach. When she hires an IT expert to save the day, she discovers he’s the same man she shared a romantic and awkward moment with at last year’s Christmas party. As they work together to recover what was lost, they may just find something even more valuable. Featuring Danielle LaRoach, Lamon Archey, Monanik Dugar and Celeste Seda. Premieres Nov. 20. ”Son of the Preacher” Jasmine, a whip-smart beauty entrepreneur, dreams of launching her own haircare brand but can’t seem to catch a break. Enter Caleb Samuel — a social-media-famous preacher’s kid with millions of followers, a fast car, and complicated family expectations. What starts as a strategic business move quickly becomes a connection that challenges them both to face love, purpose, and legacy in ways they never expected. Featuring Gabrielle Graham, Chris LeBlanc, Darren Herbert, Rachel Crawford, Ronnie Rowe, Tkaia Green and Karen Burthwright. Premieres Nov. 27. ”Love After the Holidays” A once-beloved talk show host finds herself battling alcohol addiction and personal demons that destroy everything she holds dear — her faith, her career, and even custody of her daughter. On her road to recovery, she must confront her past, repair broken relationships, and rediscover her purpose before she can truly heal. Featuring Jacinth Headlam, Malik Yoba, Jeremy Meeks, and Trina. Premieres Dec. 4. ”Never Alone for Christmas: Memphis” Two Memphis women with big hearts — a dating coach and a once-great Beale Street blues singer — find themselves unexpectedly alone for Christmas. Determined not to spend the holidays in heartbreak, they form an unlikely friendship and help each other take bold steps toward love, healing and second chances — all set to the rhythm of Memphis soul. Featuring Melissa L. Williams, Juhahn Jones, K. Michelle, Chris Sakyi, Tom Arnold, Danielle Renee Houston, Yvette Gonzalez-Nacer, Eric Lane, Timothy Tinker Sr., Kat Smith, Maurice Smith, Harold Dennis, Martel “TZ” Shaw, Sharyn Michele Grose, Walter Harris, Shelle Alycee Coleman and Kenny Young Premieres Dec. 11. ”Vera’s Holiday Flop” When Vera’s 20-year high school reunion collides with the holiday season, she braces herself for a weekend filled with awkward encounters, old flames, and plenty of bad decisions. But what starts as chaos may just lead to closure, laughter, and the kind of joy that only comes from reconnecting — and forgiving. Featuring Charity Jordan, Terri J. Vaughn, Griff, Chrissy McDaniel, Tyler Chronicles, Algebra Blessett, Jelani Akil, Scotty ATL and Saycon Sengbloh. Premieres Dec. 18. ”A Soulful Christmas” When the children of two legendary — and feuding — R&B artists are forced to collaborate on a holiday song remake, their rivalry turns into unexpected romance. But between family legacies, long-buried grudges, and a looming Christmas Eve deadline, they’ll need to find harmony both on and off the stage to create the hit that could heal two families. Featuring: Kaci Walfall, Myles Truitt, Shanice, Kenny Lattimore, Taylor Symone, E. Roger Mitchell, Towanda Braxton, KB Holland, Kyler Chavis, Gail Everett-Smith, Gerard Catus and Ryan James. Premieres Dec. 25. Hallmark ”Finding Mr. Christmas” — Season 2 Finding Mr. Christmas follows 10 aspiring actors who compete in a variety of outrageous Christmas-themed competitions to prove they have what it takes to land the next Hallmark leading role — from making gingerbread houses to physical challenges like horseback riding and skiing. Joined by beloved Hallmark guest judges each week, one contestant will be sent home for the holidays, while the winner lands a leading role in one of this year’s Countdown to Christmas movies. Featuring Jonathan Bennett and Melissa Peterman. Premiered Oct. 27, new episodes every Monday at 8 p.m. through December ”Baked with Love” In “Baked with Love: Holiday,” 10 talented pairs of home bakers face off in a warm-hearted, family-recipe bake-off. They infuse heritage, personal stories and cherished family recipes into classic bakes with a holiday twist and serve their dishes to a panel of expert judges. In the end, one pair will be crowned the Christmas Baking Champions and win the ultimate prize of $50,000 and a chance to have one of their bakes featured in a Countdown to Christmas movie. Hosted by Tamera Mowry-Housley. Premiered Oct. 27, new episodes every Monday at 9 p.m. through Dec. 15 ”Tidings for Christmas” A local newscaster falls for a single mom while learning to embrace feel-good stories at Christmas. Featuring B.J. Britt and Tamera Mowry-Housley. Premieres Nov. 16. ”The Snow Must Go On” A former Broadway actor directs a high school Christmas musical and falls for the guidance counselor. Featuring Heather Hemmens. Premieres: Nov. 28. Lifetime ”Christmas Everyday” The film follows Fancy as she tries to balance work, her family, and Christmas traditions following the death of her father. Featuring Brandy Norwood, Debbi Morgan and Sy’Rai Smith. Premieres: Nov. 29. ”The Christmas Campaign” Two rival advertising executives with completely opposite working styles are forced to team up on a festive sales pitch. As their professional ambitions collide with their personal lives, their fierce competition begins to turn into an unexpected romance. Featuring Vivica A. Fox and Jackée Harry. Premieres Nov. 29. ”Jingle All the Way to Love” Andi Kelton is on the hunt for her mystery man before Christmas. Years ago, she received a lucky sleigh bell from a handsome man at a New Year’s party. Now an established lawyer, Andi calls into a radio show to ask listeners to help her search for her dream Christmas present. Featuring Romaine Waite. Premieres Dec. 5. ”Deck the Hallways” Marie is trying one last speed dating event to find her man before Christmas. Prepared with her diary and list of dos and don’ts in hand, Marie accidentally leaves hers behind and picks up a stranger’s. Now Marie must discover if her lost diary could be the key to unlock true love in time for the holidays. Featuring Jaime M. Callica, Naika Toussaint and Loretta Devine. Premieres Dec. 6. ”A Runaway Bride for Christmas” When her wedding day did not go as planned, runaway bride Emma (Nischelle Turner) sought shelter in the place she called home. Back in her hometown, Emma reconnected with her former high school crush Mitch. But when her ex comes back to find her, she must make a tough choice between her two true loves in time for Christmas Featuring Nischelle Turner. Premieres Dec. 12. UPTv “Saving the Christmas Ranch”A woman has two days to save her family’s Christmas lodge after their accountant steals their money, while a developer makes an offer she can hardly refuse. Premieres Nov. 16. Featuring Jake Bryan-Amaning. ”A Christmas Murder Mystery” A puzzle editor spending the holidays with a wealthy family must solve a murder when one of them turns up dead. Featuring Vivica A. Fox. Premieres Dec. 7. Netflix ”My Secret Santa” A desperate single mother disguises herself as a man in order to take a seasonal job as Santa Claus. Featuring Tia Mowry. Premieres Dec. 3. OWN ”Fake Yourself a Merry Little Christmas”When reserved professor Maya tells a little white lie about being in a relationship with an unconscious stranger, she never expects to get swept up in the stranger’s family’s holiday plans. Things are made even more complicated by her undeniable chemistry with her “boyfriend’s” doctor, Daniel, who just so happens to be her ex. Featuring Kiki Layne and Etienne Maurice. Premieres Nov. 29. ”The Christmas Showdown” Former childhood best friends, April and Chastity, haven’t spoken ever since April bailed on their plan to move to New York, choosing Paris instead to chase her dream as an event producer. When her career fizzles, April returns home and unexpectedly crosses paths with Chastity, who is also out of work, and desperate for a fresh start. Both women set their sights on the same event design job for the upcoming Sugar Heights Christmas Eve Spectacular. But to impress Hen, the event producer overseeing the show, they’ll need to mend old wounds and work as a team. What begins as a friendly rivalry, quickly escalates to an all-out holiday showdown. Featuring Amber Stevens West, Corbin Reid, Loretta Devine, Obba Babatunde and Carla Renata. Premiers Dec. 6. ”Very Merry Mystery” Known for her unmatched hairstyling skills and her infectious love of Christmas, beloved beauty shop owner Bea is the bedrock of Goldfern, GA. When she attends a Christmas Murder Mystery party at the mansion of a hard-nosed businesswoman, the evening takes a shocking turn when the host goes missing and a ransom note is found. To solve the crime, Bea must team up with her boyfriend, Troy , who is also a newly promoted detective. Featuring Ashleigh Murray and Tristan Mack Wilds. Premieres Dec. 13. The Roku Channel ”Merry Little Mystery” In this holiday rom-com Jordin Sparks plays Natasha Maxwell, who tries to foil a determined reporter’s (Keon Alexander) attempts to reveal her identity as the benevolent Secret Santa of a small town...and ends up falling in love. Audiences can also look forward to a brand-new original song by Sparks, created exclusively for the film. Featuring Jordin Sparks and Keon Alexander. Premieres Nov. 19. ”Honest Renovations: A Holiday Home Makeover” Mathis along with Jessica Alba sets their sights on transforming the home of a heroic fire captain who bravely battled the devastating Los Angeles wildfires earlier this year. Featuring Lizzy Mathis. Premieres Nov. 8. ”The Great American Baking Show: Celebrity Holiday” For its fourth season, “The Great American Baking Show: Celebrity Holiday” returns with a new lineup of celebrity bakers. Judges Paul Hollywood and Prue Leith will take on the new batch of celebrity bakers alongside hosts Casey Wilson and the newly added Andrew Rannells. Premieres Nov. 3. Prime Video ”Tyler Perry’s Finding Joy” A talented but undervalued fashion designer from New York City follows her crush to Colorado during the holidays. However, a shocking turn of events leaves her stranded in a snowstorm, where she meets a mysterious stranger who challenges her perspective on life and love. Featuring Shannon Thornton, Tosin Morohunfola, Brittany S. Hall, Inayah, Eric, Stanton Betts, Aaron O’Connell, Natalie O’Connell, Jeffery Thomas Johnson and Whitney Goin. Premieres Nov. 5. ”Oh. What. Fun.” When her family accidentally leaves her behind during the holidays, a devoted mom embarks on an impromptu adventure. Featuring Danielle Brooks. Premieres Dec. 3. Beauty, and More Here’s a look at some steal-worthy ideas we spotted in November 2025. Claire Hoffman , Senior Contributing Editor November 25, 2025 14 Min Read e.l.f. Photo: Tory Stolper Photography Once a month, BizBash brings you even more inspiration for your own gatherings with our "Cool Event Ideas of the Month" column, where we round up some of the creative ideas we haven\'t had the chance to cover yet. Our November 2025 roundup includes L.L.Bean\'s cozy ode to flannel, e.l.f. Beauty\'s custom donation kiosk, Uber Eats Canada’s data-driven hockey activation, and Absolut\'s eye-catching bar at the Wicked: For Good premiere. Scroll on to see these and more from brands like Kate Spade, Hello Sunshine, and Disney+. L.L.Bean NYC Residency From Oct. 18 through Nov. 30, L.L.Bean has brought its six-week residency to New York City, inviting guests into an immersive space centered on the comfort and nostalgia of flannel. Open Wednesday through Sunday each week, the residency encourages visitors to explore, personalize, and discover timeless classics, with weekly expansions into sweaters, outerwear, holiday essentials, and cold-weather accessories. Photo: Sara Kerens Programming throughout the residency has included free embroidery by Abbode, a whimsical Halloween lineup with movie screenings and themed mocktails, exclusive Harris Tweed pieces, a curated vintage selection from Wooden Sleepers, and holiday gift-giving moments featuring refreshments and a charm bar. The rotating assortment and seasonal touchpoints offers guests new discoveries with each visit. Photo: Sara Karens The residency was produced by Factory360 . Photo: Sarah Kerens Hello Sunshine’s Sunniefest On Nov. 15 at Pegasus Park in Dallas, Hello Sunshine hosted its inaugural Sunniefest, an immersive festival co-created with Gen Z girls to spark connection, creativity, and self-expression. Produced by Mirrored Media , the full-day program featured conversations with next-gen talent—including Jacey Adler, Marley Dias, Kiernan Shipka, Neha Shukla, and others—alongside hands-on workshops, bespoke activations, and branded pop-ups designed to inspire and empower attendees. Photo: Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images for Hello Sunshine Cozy seating complemented a lineup of workshops led by creators, advocates, and Hello Sunshine Collective members, plus interactive offerings from partners like Coach, Victoria’s Secret PINK, and e.l.f. Beauty. The festival also marked the launch of Sunnie Reads, a new Gen Z–driven book club developed in partnership with Coach. Photo: Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images for Hello Sunshine The festival’s STEM Lab, presented by Lyda Hill Philanthropies’ IF/THEN initiative, invited attendees to dive into scent science, robotics, and hands-on experimentation with guidance from AAAS IF/THEN ambassadors Jenn Makins and Dr. Jennifer Stimpson. Nearby, Purdue University encouraged girls to explore future career paths through a photo-ready mural, postcard wall, and a session with AI expert and faculty member Kasie Roberson, PhD. Photo: Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images for Hello Sunshine e.l.f. Beauty\'s “Give an e.l.f.” Pop-Up On Oct. 28 in New York, e.l.f. Beauty hosted an all-day pop-up at Astor Place and Lafayette Street to mark the release of its fourth annual Impact Report and celebrate its “Give an e.l.f.” campaign. Nearly 1,000 community members stopped by to make their values count by selecting a cause at a custom donation kiosk—triggering a donation from e.l.f.—and redeeming their receipt at a gift bar for products. Photo: Tory Stolper Photography Across the activation, e.l.f. contributed $50,000 to six nonprofits chosen by the community: RISE, the It Gets Better Project, Look Good Feel Better, Best Friends Animal Society, and the Billie Jean King Foundation. The Bait Shoppe handled creative, production, and fabrication for the pop-up. Photo: Tory Stolper Photography Balloon Museum’s “Pop Air—Art Is Inflatable” Exhibition On Nov. 15 in Houston, the Balloon Museum opened "Pop Air—Art Is Inflatable," a large-scale exhibition created by Italy-based Lux Entertainment . Spanning more than 65,000 square feet, the showcase—which runs through April 2026—brings together luminous displays, interactive environments, and inflatable installations from 14 international artists, inviting visitors of all ages to explore the intersection of art, air, and play. Photo: Courtesy of Balloon Museum Featured works include Cyril Lancelin’s "Crazy Love for Polygons," Hyperstudio’s "Glowing Ballet," "10 Agosto," and "Hypercosmo," "Soft Hurricane" by Quiet Ensemble, ENESS’s "Spiritus Sonata," Karina Smigla-Bobinski’s "ADA," and Max Streicher’s "Silenius." The exhibition also incorporates digital experiences like Ultravioletto’s VR installation and Pepper’s Ghost’s ARIA infinity room, alongside participatory works from MOTOREFISICO (pictured), Pneuhaus & Bike Powered Events, Jimmy Kuehnle, Rub Kandy, and Filthy Luker. Photo: Courtesy of Balloon Museum Uber Eats Canada’s "Crave the Stats" Activation To celebrate hockey home openers in Toronto and Vancouver, Uber Eats Canada launched Crave the Stats, a data-driven activation that turned game-day food habits into part of the stat sheet. Outside Scotiabank Arena and Rogers Arena, the brand set up massive Uber Eats bags—20 feet tall in Toronto and 16 feet tall in Vancouver—inviting fans to engage with food-and-hockey trivia while spotlighting ordering trends from the 2024–2025 season. Photo: Courtesy of Uber Eats Canada Fans lined up for interactive challenges and on-the-spot prizes, including Uber Eats vouchers, game-night tickets, signed merch, and meet-and-greets with hockey legends Darcy Tucker and Chris Higgins. The builds drew thousands of participants across both markets and generated more than 2.3 million influencer impressions, surpassing category engagement benchmarks. Photo: Courtesy of Uber Eats Canada The campaign was created by T1 , with fabrication by MAWG and media by Touche! Photo: Courtesy of Uber Eats Canada Kate Spade New York x NYLON “Holiday Duo-ets” On Nov. 4 in Los Angeles, Kate Spade New York and NYLON transformed the Chateau Marmont Penthouse into a wintery, music-filled setting for “Holiday Duo-ets,” a celebration of togetherness and the spirit of gifting. Guests enjoyed festive cocktails, piano sing-alongs, and an immersive holiday environment anchored by a snow sculpture of the brand’s signature Duo bag. Photo: Nina Fernandez/BFA.com Inside, framed photos of guests at the event were used as tree ornaments. Brand ambassadors Ice Spice and Laufey led the evening, joined by Reign Judge, NYLON members, and attendees who included Kelsey Anderson, Rachael Kirkconnell, Baron Schoenvogel, Zoi Lerma, and more. The event was inspired by Kate Spade New York’s “Spark Something Beautiful” holiday campaign. Photo: Nina Fernandez/BFA.com TIRTIR’s “Radiant Pop-Up” On Nov. 14 in Los Angeles, global K-beauty brand TIRTIR debuted its immersive “Radiant Pop-Up” on Melrose Avenue. The installation marks a major moment for the brand—introducing a new logo, announcing global ambassador V, and bringing its “Your Shade, Our Standard” campaign to life through the experiential concept “V&You, Let’s Radiate.” A pre-opening event welcomed celebrities, influencers, and media. Photo: Courtesy of TIRTIR Inside the pop-up, guests could explore TIRTIR’s core complexion and skincare lineup, including the Mask Fit Red Cushion Foundation, Mask Fit AI Filter Cushion, Waterism Glow Tint, Milk Skin Toner, Matcha Skin Toner, and the new Banana BDRN. Interactive zones were designed to let visitors test textures, performance, and formulations firsthand while showcasing the brand’s updated aesthetic and identity. Photo: Courtesy of TIRTIR The pop-up ran through Nov. 23 and served as the starting point for additional experiential activations planned across major North American cities as the brand continues to grow its presence. Photo: Courtesy of TIRTIR The Owen’s Mixery at Warped Tour Orlando At Warped Tour Orlando, Owen’s Craft Mixers brought The Owen’s Mixery to life, marking the first in-person activation tied to MGK’s new role as the brand’s creative taste officer. Before his headlining set, MGK stopped by to pour mocktails and meet fans, drawing a crowd and highlighting the brand’s connection to music and fan culture. Photo: Courtesy of Owen’s Craft Mixers The Mixery aimed to reimagine the typical festival bar with custom cocktail and mocktail builds guided by an on-site mixologist, a window-service bar, and a playful “Owen the Mule” photo moment. The activation is part of Owen’s expanding partnership with Live Nation, spanning more than 100 venues and festivals nationwide. Photo: Courtesy of Owen’s Craft Mixers Absolut Activation at the Wicked: For Good Premiere Last week, 160over90 ’s experiential team supported Absolut at the NYC premiere of Wicked: For Good . As the film’s official partner, Absolut activated on the red carpet with a six-foot bar and back bar positioned along the press line, appearing prominently as cast members arrived and conducted interviews. Photo: Courtesy of 160over90 The setup showcased the limited-edition Absolut bottle in a pink-and-green sequin sleeve, and guests sampled themed cocktails including the Absolut x Ozmopolitan, Absolut x Thrillifying! Twist, and the Absolut & Kahlúa x Ozpresso Martini. Photo: Courtesy of 160over90 PatPat’s Holiday Movie Lounge On Nov. 12 in West Hollywood, families kicked off the season at PatPat’s Holiday Movie Lounge at E.P. & L.P.’s Melrose Rooftop Theatre. The event brought together families and celebrity guests—including Audrina Patridge, Chanel West Coast, Amber Stevens West, Anna Maria Perez de Tagle, Taylor Selfridge, Chelsea Tavares, Caroline D’Amore, Joey Tierney, and Danielle Ruiz—for a cozy evening of crafts, treats, and holiday fun hosted by the kids and family apparel brand. Photo: Stephanie Loren Photography Guests settled in beneath the stars for a rooftop screening of Disney’s Frozen , many wearing matching PatPat Disney sweaters and family pajamas to mark the start of the holidays. Photo: Stephanie Loren Photography Gravity One’s “First Round’s On Us” Activation Outside Adweek Brandweek in Atlanta, Gravity One —a new division of Gravity Global focused on breakthrough B2C work—staged a tongue-in-cheek guerrilla activation aimed directly at marketing decision-makers. A digital truck parked at the venue entrance flashed the message “IS YOUR BRAND WEAK?”, directing attendees to BrandWeak.com to enter for a chance to win a free first round of brand work, including strategy and creative. Photo: Courtesy of Gravity One Pro Padel League’s 2025 City’s Cup Finals Held Oct. 16-19 in Manhattan, the Pro Padel League’s 2025 City’s Cup Finals transformed the Hammerstein Ballroom into a full-scale padel arena for more than 5,000 fans. The four-day tournament featured matches with top-ranked players, culminating in the New York Atlantics taking home the season-long title. GSE Worldwide produced the event, with broadcast and streaming by MediaPro and court design by AFP Courts . Photo: GSE Worldwide To reimagine the concert venue for competition, GSE Worldwide tapped Beyond Merritt Design to handle event design across the lobby, promenade, and VIP seating areas. Custom floor-to-ceiling graphics, backlit SEGs, and branded balcony banners gave the ballroom an arena-like feel, while VIP zones featured modern lounges, a 56-foot media wall, and suites outfitted with tailored seating. Crossfire AV handled audiovisual, PM1 provided stadium seating, and United Rentals supplied power. Photo: GSE Worldwide Throughout the four days, guests encountered immersive touchpoints designed for both the in-person and on-camera experience—from backdrops for broadcast interviews to lounges furnished with boucle sofas, brass tables, and taupe velvet armchairs. Great Performances catered bites from Flyfish Club and Capon’s Burgers, while Foxtenn supported live scoring and VAR, Komo Technologies oversaw fan engagement, and multimedia elements from artist Erik Mednis rounded out the production. Photo: GSE Worldwide The Glam & Glowtel by Shark Beauty On Oct. 25-26 at The Grove in Los Angeles, Shark Beauty partnered with CNC Agency to transform The Park into The Glowtel, a hotel-inspired pop-up celebrating the brand’s latest beauty-tech innovations. Guests checked in for express self-care rituals across immersive suites—including the Hair Suite and Skin Suite—where they experienced guided 10-minute treatments with the FlexStyle, SmoothStyle, and CryoGlow LED Mask. Photo: CNC Agency The activation featured key fob gamification, lounge-style photo moments, on-site shopping, and appearances from influencers, all designed to reimagine beauty as approachable luxury. Over the weekend, The Glowtel drew thousands of visitors and generated strong social engagement around Shark Beauty’s growing portfolio. Photo CNC Agency UCLA Mattel Children’s Hospital’s 25th Party on the Pier On Nov. 2 in Santa Monica, UCLA Mattel Children’s Hospital marked the 25th anniversary of its Party on the Pier fund-raiser at Pacific Park on the Santa Monica Pier. Produced by 1540 Productions , the event brought families, community supporters, and a roster of celebrity guests for a four-hour celebration benefiting pediatric programs across the hospital’s locations. Photo: Line 8 Photography Guests spent the day enjoying unlimited access to Pacific Park rides, plus carnival games stocked with prizes from Mattel Inc. The event also featured meal vouchers, classic pier snacks, and the “Power of Play” craft tent sponsored by The Goldhirsh-Yellin Foundation, along with photo activations and celebrity meet-and-greets. Photo: Line 8 Photography There was also a VIP area sponsored by the Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation. In another space, therapy dogs from UCLA’s People-Animal Connection added a comforting presence throughout the pier, rounding out a day designed to raise critical unrestricted funds for high-priority pediatric programs. Photo: Line 8 Photography Disney+ Halloween Fest On Oct. 25 in Burbank, Disney+ hosted its Halloween Fest at The Walt Disney Studios, where kids, families, and stars from popular Disney shows arrived in costume for an evening of performances, games, rides, and trick-or-treating across the studio lot. Photo: Disney/Richard Harbaugh The celebration also featured a costume contest and appearances from special celebrity guests, creating a festive, family-friendly atmosphere against the backdrop of the iconic studio grounds. Photo: Disney/Richard Harbaugh Produced by Mirrored Media , the event also featured carnival games inspired by Disney+ shows. Photo: Disney/Richard Harbaugh Saatva and Team USA: Special Athlete Roundtable On Oct. 27 in New York City, mattress company Saatva hosted a roundtable at its Flatiron Viewing Room to commemorate its partnership with Team USA and the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Moderated by former NBC Sports anchor Dave Briggs, the conversation featured athletes Brenna Huckaby and Noah Elliott (Para snowboarding) and Lauren Macuga (alpine skiing), drawing media, partners, and design enthusiasts for an evening centered on connection and the role of restorative sleep in elite performance. Photo: Nicolette Francis The event embraced the Italian tradition of la tavola with storytelling, aperitivo-style bites from Alimentari Flaneur , and florals by Laura Hurst . Vendors included Taylor Creative and propNspoon for rentals, Forrest Sound and Vision for AV, and Lucy Blossoms for photo moments, rounding out a milestone moment for Saatva as the Official Mattress and Restorative Sleep Provider of Team USA and LA28. Photo: Nicolette Francis Visit Tucson’s Chicago Pop-Up On Nov. 15 in Chicago, Visit Tucson partnered with GDX Studios and Madden Media to bring a slice of Tucson’s Mexican food scene to Millennium Park. With Halloween and all things spooky officially come to an end, it’s that time of year for holiday films. From Hallmark to Lifetime, streaming services like Netflix and beyond, viewers can expect heartwarming stories with happy endings set against beautiful backdrops, along with delightful cooking shows. This guide will help you get into the holiday spirit. BET+ ”Christmas By Design” A famous handbag designer working on a special-edition holiday line for charity finds her newest designs stolen in a company data breach. When she hires an IT expert to save the day, she discovers he’s the same man she shared a romantic and awkward moment with at last year’s Christmas party. As they work together to recover what was lost, they may just find something even more valuable. Featuring Danielle LaRoach, Lamon Archey, Monanik Dugar and Celeste Seda. Premieres Nov. 20. ”Son of the Preacher” Jasmine, a whip-smart beauty entrepreneur, dreams of launching her own haircare brand but can’t seem to catch a break. Enter Caleb Samuel — a social-media-famous preacher’s kid with millions of followers, a fast car, and complicated family expectations. What starts as a strategic business move quickly becomes a connection that challenges them both to face love, purpose, and legacy in ways they never expected. Featuring Gabrielle Graham, Chris LeBlanc, Darren Herbert, Rachel Crawford, Ronnie Rowe, Tkaia Green and Karen Burthwright. Premieres Nov. 27. ”Love After the Holidays” A once-beloved talk show host finds herself battling alcohol addiction and personal demons that destroy everything she holds dear — her faith, her career, and even custody of her daughter. On her road to recovery, she must confront her past, repair broken relationships, and rediscover her purpose before she can truly heal. Featuring Jacinth Headlam, Malik Yoba, Jeremy Meeks, and Trina. Premieres Dec. 4. ”Never Alone for Christmas: Memphis” Two Memphis women with big hearts — a dating coach and a once-great Beale Street blues singer — find themselves unexpectedly alone for Christmas. Determined not to spend the holidays in heartbreak, they form an unlikely friendship and help each other take bold steps toward love, healing and second chances — all set to the rhythm of Memphis soul. Featuring Melissa L. Williams, Juhahn Jones, K. Michelle, Chris Sakyi, Tom Arnold, Danielle Renee Houston, Yvette Gonzalez-Nacer, Eric Lane, Timothy Tinker Sr., Kat Smith, Maurice Smith, Harold Dennis, Martel “TZ” Shaw, Sharyn Michele Grose, Walter Harris, Shelle Alycee Coleman and Kenny Young Premieres Dec. 11. ”Vera’s Holiday Flop” When Vera’s 20-year high school reunion collides with the holiday season, she braces herself for a weekend filled with awkward encounters, old flames, and plenty of bad decisions. But what starts as chaos may just lead to closure, laughter, and the kind of joy that only comes from reconnecting — and forgiving. Featuring Charity Jordan, Terri J. Vaughn, Griff, Chrissy McDaniel, Tyler Chronicles, Algebra Blessett, Jelani Akil, Scotty ATL and Saycon Sengbloh. Premieres Dec. 18. ”A Soulful Christmas” When the children of two legendary — and feuding — R&B artists are forced to collaborate on a holiday song remake, their rivalry turns into unexpected romance. But between family legacies, long-buried grudges, and a looming Christmas Eve deadline, they’ll need to find harmony both on and off the stage to create the hit that could heal two families. Featuring: Kaci Walfall, Myles Truitt, Shanice, Kenny Lattimore, Taylor Symone, E. Roger Mitchell, Towanda Braxton, KB Holland, Kyler Chavis, Gail Everett-Smith, Gerard Catus and Ryan James. Premieres Dec. 25. Hallmark ”Finding Mr. Christmas” — Season 2 Finding Mr. Christmas follows 10 aspiring actors who compete in a variety of outrageous Christmas-themed competitions to prove they have what it takes to land the next Hallmark leading role — from making gingerbread houses to physical challenges like horseback riding and skiing. Joined by beloved Hallmark guest judges each week, one contestant will be sent home for the holidays, while the winner lands a leading role in one of this year’s Countdown to Christmas movies. Featuring Jonathan Bennett and Melissa Peterman. Premiered Oct. 27, new episodes every Monday at 8 p.m. through December ”Baked with Love” In “Baked with Love: Holiday,” 10 talented pairs of home bakers face off in a warm-hearted, family-recipe bake-off. They infuse heritage, personal stories and cherished family recipes into classic bakes with a holiday twist and serve their dishes to a panel of expert judges. In the end, one pair will be crowned the Christmas Baking Champions and win the ultimate prize of $50,000 and a chance to have one of their bakes featured in a Countdown to Christmas movie. Hosted by Tamera Mowry-Housley. Premiered Oct. 27, new episodes every Monday at 9 p.m. through Dec. 15 ”Tidings for Christmas” A local newscaster falls for a single mom while learning to embrace feel-good stories at Christmas. Featuring B.J. Britt and Tamera Mowry-Housley. Premieres Nov. 16. ”The Snow Must Go On” A former Broadway actor directs a high school Christmas musical and falls for the guidance counselor. Featuring Heather Hemmens. Premieres: Nov. 28. Lifetime ”Christmas Everyday” The film follows Fancy as she tries to balance work, her family, and Christmas traditions following the death of her father. Featuring Brandy Norwood, Debbi Morgan and Sy’Rai Smith. Premieres: Nov. 29. ”The Christmas Campaign” Two rival advertising executives with completely opposite working styles are forced to team up on a festive sales pitch. As their professional ambitions collide with their personal lives, their fierce competition begins to turn into an unexpected romance. Featuring Vivica A. Fox and Jackée Harry. Premieres Nov. 29. ”Jingle All the Way to Love” Andi Kelton is on the hunt for her mystery man before Christmas. Years ago, she received a lucky sleigh bell from a handsome man at a New Year’s party. Now an established lawyer, Andi calls into a radio show to ask listeners to help her search for her dream Christmas present. Featuring Romaine Waite. Premieres Dec. 5. ”Deck the Hallways” Marie is trying one last speed dating event to find her man before Christmas. Prepared with her diary and list of dos and don’ts in hand, Marie accidentally leaves hers behind and picks up a stranger’s. Now Marie must discover if her lost diary could be the key to unlock true love in time for the holidays. Featuring Jaime M. Callica, Naika Toussaint and Loretta Devine. Premieres Dec. 6. ”A Runaway Bride for Christmas” When her wedding day did not go as planned, runaway bride Emma (Nischelle Turner) sought shelter in the place she called home. Back in her hometown, Emma reconnected with her former high school crush Mitch. But when her ex comes back to find her, she must make a tough choice between her two true loves in time for Christmas Featuring Nischelle Turner. Premieres Dec. 12. UPTv “Saving the Christmas Ranch”A woman has two days to save her family’s Christmas lodge after their accountant steals their money, while a developer makes an offer she can hardly refuse. Premieres Nov. 16. Featuring Jake Bryan-Amaning. ”A Christmas Murder Mystery” A puzzle editor spending the holidays with a wealthy family must solve a murder when one of them turns up dead. Featuring Vivica A. Fox. Premieres Dec. 7. Netflix ”My Secret Santa” A desperate single mother disguises herself as a man in order to take a seasonal job as Santa Claus. Featuring Tia Mowry. Premieres Dec. 3. OWN ”Fake Yourself a Merry Little Christmas”When reserved professor Maya tells a little white lie about being in a relationship with an unconscious stranger, she never expects to get swept up in the stranger’s family’s holiday plans. Things are made even more complicated by her undeniable chemistry with her “boyfriend’s” doctor, Daniel, who just so happens to be her ex. Featuring Kiki Layne and Etienne Maurice. Premieres Nov. 29. ”The Christmas Showdown” Former childhood best friends, April and Chastity, haven’t spoken ever since April bailed on their plan to move to New York, choosing Paris instead to chase her dream as an event producer. When her career fizzles, April returns home and unexpectedly crosses paths with Chastity, who is also out of work, and desperate for a fresh start. Both women set their sights on the same event design job for the upcoming Sugar Heights Christmas Eve Spectacular. But to impress Hen, the event producer overseeing the show, they’ll need to mend old wounds and work as a team. What begins as a friendly rivalry, quickly escalates to an all-out holiday showdown. Featuring Amber Stevens West, Corbin Reid, Loretta Devine, Obba Babatunde and Carla Renata. Premiers Dec. 6. ”Very Merry Mystery” Known for her unmatched hairstyling skills and her infectious love of Christmas, beloved beauty shop owner Bea is the bedrock of Goldfern, GA. When she attends a Christmas Murder Mystery party at the mansion of a hard-nosed businesswoman, the evening takes a shocking turn when the host goes missing and a ransom note is found. To solve the crime, Bea must team up with her boyfriend, Troy , who is also a newly promoted detective. Featuring Ashleigh Murray and Tristan Mack Wilds. Premieres Dec. 13. The Roku Channel ”Merry Little Mystery” In this holiday rom-com Jordin Sparks plays Natasha Maxwell, who tries to foil a determined reporter’s (Keon Alexander) attempts to reveal her identity as the benevolent Secret Santa of a small town...and ends up falling in love. Audiences can also look forward to a brand-new original song by Sparks, created exclusively for the film. Featuring Jordin Sparks and Keon Alexander. Premieres Nov. 19. ”Honest Renovations: A Holiday Home Makeover” Mathis along with Jessica Alba sets their sights on transforming the home of a heroic fire captain who bravely battled the devastating Los Angeles wildfires earlier this year. Featuring Lizzy Mathis. Premieres Nov. 8. ”The Great American Baking Show: Celebrity Holiday” For its fourth season, “The Great American Baking Show: Celebrity Holiday” returns with a new lineup of celebrity bakers. Judges Paul Hollywood and Prue Leith will take on the new batch of celebrity bakers alongside hosts Casey Wilson and the newly added Andrew Rannells. Premieres Nov. 3. Prime Video ”Tyler Perry’s Finding Joy” A talented but undervalued fashion designer from New York City follows her crush to Colorado during the holidays. However, a shocking turn of events leaves her stranded in a snowstorm, where she meets a mysterious stranger who challenges her perspective on life and love. Featuring Shannon Thornton, Tosin Morohunfola, Brittany S. Hall, Inayah, Eric, Stanton Betts, Aaron O’Connell, Natalie O’Connell, Jeffery Thomas Johnson and Whitney Goin. Premieres Nov. 5. ”Oh. What. Fun.” When her family accidentally leaves her behind during the holidays, a devoted mom embarks on an impromptu adventure. Featuring Danielle Brooks. Premieres Dec. 3. Between interviews I’ve conducted myself and blogs done by my colleagues here at CRACKED , I now know more about Matt and Trey than I do some of my own family members—which I am entirely fine with. As such, here are five things I’ve learned about Matt Stone and Trey Parker just by being a part of this website. 5 Trey Parker Flunked Out of College Matt Stone and Trey Parker met while students at the University of Colorado at Boulder. They were in a film class and began making movies together. Cannibal! the Musical was their crowning achievement. Parker dropped out of college because of how much time he dedicated to the film and told Dennis Miller in 1998, “I only got kicked out of school because I was working so hard on this film, trying to get it done, and failed all my classes.” 4 Trey Parker Knew Butters Before Matt Stone South Park producer Eric Stough , who served as inspiration for Butters, was two years behind Trey Parker in school and recalled his introduction to the South Park co-creator. “I think I first saw him in junior high at West Jefferson Elementary School. I was in the audience, and they were doing a talent show,” Stough began. “Trey had a band, and they did this fake band called ‘Satan’s Offspring,’ making fun of heavy metal. They were playing things like the Andy Griffith song, but heavy rock style, and they smashed their guitars and stuff like that. It caused this big uprising because all the heavy metal-ers were upset that Trey was making fun of them. Later, I remember being on the school bus and watching his parents get him out of school because they wanted him to be safe.” Advertisement 3 They Couldn’t Function with a Traditional Writers Room Comedy Central mandated South Park utilize a traditional writer’s room process during the show’s first season, which Matt Stone and Trey Parker eventually terminated. Advertisement In my roundtable with three writers who attended the ill-fated experiment, Dave Polsky, said “I didn’t know enough to know how odd this was, but we met once a week for a few hours. We’d be told what time and we showed up for that time, but we didn’t see a lot of them. There was no rhythm to it. I found it hard to get my footing.” According to writer Phil Stark, Stone and Parker told Comedy Central “We don’t want to do it like this,” at the end of the first season. 2 They’re Workaholics Advertisement Those three writers all made a point to say that Stone and Parker were never unkind or disrespectful towards them, but showed their affection in juvenile ways. Dan Sterling explained, “I knew I felt better when Matt was farting on me on a regular basis.” Advertisement Still, it was clear that Stone and Parker had a tight focus on work. Stark said “They aren’t the kind of guys who walk in and say, ‘Hey, how’s your weekend?’ Matt a little bit more, but Trey definitely isn’t.” Mona Marshall and April Stewart held the same sentiment. Stewart mentioned how kind Stone and Parker were to her over the years and especially during her pregnancy, but also confirmed their devotion to the show. As Marshall put it, “They’re focused on the work, but not to the extent that they’re jerks.” 1 Trey Parker and Matt Stone Don’t Do Projects Apart From Each Other Finally, I’ve learned why Matt Stone and Trey Parker don’t do solo projects , despite receiving many offers. In the documentary Six Days to Air , Matt Stone explained “Even though we’re a partnership, the way that the stories, either in South Park or the movies, are expressed is completely through Trey. Like, Trey’s the chef.” Advertisement Stone continued, saying “...I’ve got channels through him. Or, where I can get to be tough is exactly where Trey’s not. And where he can be tough is exactly where I’m not. You won’t get in an argument with Trey; Trey’s not going to argue with you about some things. as well as on Digital. The 4K Ultra HD Combo Pack features an Ultra HD Blu-ray disc in 4K with HDR, a Blu-ray disc featuring the film in hi-definition, and a digital version of the movie. The Blu-ray Combo Pack features a Blu-ray disc with the film in hi-definition, a DVD with the film in standard definition, and a digital version of the movie. It’s the dawn of a new age of heroes, and Metropolis has just met its first. But as Daily Planet intern Clark Kent – working alongside reporter Lois Lane – secretly wields his alien powers of flight, super-strength and x-ray vision in the battle for good, there’s even greater trouble on the horizon. Follow the budding hero as he engages in bloody battles with intergalactic bounty hunter Lobo and fights for his life to halt the attack of power-hungry alien Parasite. The world will learn about Superman … but first, Superman must save the world! Emmy and Golden Globe Award winner Darren Criss ( Glee, American Crime Story: The Assassination of Gianni Versace ) and Emmy nominee Zachary Quinto ( Star Trek franchise, Heroes ) lead a star-studded cast as the voices of Superman/Clark Kent and Lex Luthor, respectively. The cast also includes Alexandra Daddario ( San Andreas, Baywatch, All My Children ) as Lois Lane, Brett Dalton ( Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. ) as Parasite/Rudy Jones, Ryan Hurst ( The Walking Dead, Sons of Anarchy, Remember the Titans ) as Lobo, Ike Amadi ( Mass Effect 3, Mortal Kombat Legends: Scorpion’s Revenge ) as Martian Manhunter, Neil Flynn ( The Middle, Scrubs ) as Jonathan Kent, Bellamy Young ( Scandal, Prodigal Son ) as Martha Kent, Cristina Milizia ( DC Super Hero Girls ) as Maya, Petey & Kaylie, Eugene Byrd ( Bones, LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures ) as Ron Troupe, April Stewart ( South Park ) as Mrs. Ross, and Piotr Michael ( The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle ) as Perry White, as well as Cissy Jones ( Firewatch ) and David Chen ( Gotham ). Superman: Man of Tomorrow introduces a new producing vision to the DC Universe Movies series, which now numbers 41 films over its 13 years of existence. Supervising Producer Butch Lukic has a rich pedigree in DC animated productions, serving as producer on Constantine: City of Demons , Justice League Action and the Batman Unlimited franchise, as well as directing episodes of Justice League , Batman Beyond and Beware the Batman . Lukic brings a new visual aesthetic to Superman: Man of Tomorrow that departs from the animation styles – of previous producers Bruce Timm (23 films) and James Tucker (17 films) – thus far represented in the DC Universe Movies . See also Marvel Studios Releases Special Look At Upcoming Movies Chris Palmer ( Voltron: Legendary Defender ) is the director of Superman: Man of Tomorrow , utilizing a script by Tim Sheridan ( The Death of Superman ). Producers are Jim Krieg ( Batman: Gotham by Gaslight ) and Kimberly S. Moreau ( Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles ). Executive Producer is Sam Register. “ Superman: Man of Tomorrow is an inspiring retelling of the DC Universe Movies ’ backstory for The Man of Steel, taking the audience to his early days as an intern at the Daily Planet – and his beginnings as a learning-on-the-job DC Super Hero,” said Mary Ellen Thomas, Warner Bros. Home Entertainment Senior Vice President, Originals, Animation and Family Marketing. “Darren Criss and Zachary Quinto have wholeheartedly embraced their roles as Superman and Lex Luthor for this film, and the end result is a special addition to canon of films that every Superman fan will want to add to their collection.” Superman: Man of Tomorrow Special Features 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Combo Pack, Blu-ray Combo Pack and Digital Lobo: Natural Force of Chaos (New Featurette) – He’s the rude, crude, galactic bounty hunter who has been more than a thorn in the side of DC’s greatest heroes. This is a full throttle look at Lobo. Martian Manhunter: Lost and Found (New Featurette) – This is the personal journey of J’onn J’onzz. A stranger in a strange land who emerges from the shadows as a force for peace and justice. Look Back: Justice League vs. The Fatal Five (Featurette) – The Earth’s future hangs in the balance when the Justice League faces a powerful new threat – the Fatal Five. Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman seek answers as the time-traveling trio of Mano, Persuader and Tharok terrorize Metropolis in search of budding Green Lantern, Jessica Cruz – whom they need to be able to free remaining Fatal Five members Emerald Empress and Validus in order to carry out their sinister plan. But the Justice League discover an ally from another time in the peculiar Star Boy – brimming with volatile power, could he be the key to thwarting the Fatal Five? An epic battle against ultimate evil awaits! Look Back: Superman/Batman: Public Enemies (Featurette) – Based on the popular Jeph Loeb/Ed McGuinness comic series/graphic novel, the film finds United States President Lex Luthor using the oncoming trajectory of a Kryptonite asteroid to frame Superman and declare a $1 billion bounty on the heads of the Man of Steel and his “partner in crime,” Batman. Heroes and villains alike launch a relentless pursuit of Superman and Batman, who must unite – and recruit help – to stave off the action-packed onslaught, stop the asteroid, and uncover Luthor’s devious plot to take command of far more than North America. posted on August 23, 2020 @ 2:49 pm Superman: Man of Tomorrow will be available on 4K Ultra HD Combo Pack (USA $39.99 SRP; Canada $44.98 SRP) and Blu-ray Combo Pack (USA $24.98 SRP; Canada $29.98 SRP) as well as on Digital. The 4K Ultra HD Combo Pack features an Ultra HD Blu-ray disc in 4K with HDR, a Blu-ray disc featuring the film in hi-definition, and a digital version of the movie. The Blu-ray Combo Pack features a Blu-ray disc with the film in hi-definition, a DVD with the film in standard definition, and a digital version of the movie. It’s the dawn of a new age of heroes, and Metropolis has just met its first. But as Daily Planet intern Clark Kent – working alongside reporter Lois Lane – secretly wields his alien powers of flight, super-strength and x-ray vision in the battle for good, there’s even greater trouble on the horizon. Follow the budding hero as he engages in bloody battles with intergalactic bounty hunter Lobo and fights for his life to halt the attack of power-hungry alien Parasite. The world will learn about Superman … but first, Superman must save the world! Emmy and Golden Globe Award winner Darren Criss ( Glee, American Crime Story: The Assassination of Gianni Versace ) and Emmy nominee Zachary Quinto ( Star Trek franchise, Heroes ) lead a star-studded cast as the voices of Superman/Clark Kent and Lex Luthor, respectively. The cast also includes Alexandra Daddario ( San Andreas, Baywatch, All My Children ) as Lois Lane, Brett Dalton ( Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. ) as Parasite/Rudy Jones, Ryan Hurst ( The Walking Dead, Sons of Anarchy, Remember the Titans ) as Lobo, Ike Amadi ( Mass Effect 3, Mortal Kombat Legends: Scorpion’s Revenge ) as Martian Manhunter, Neil Flynn ( The Middle, Scrubs ) as Jonathan Kent, Bellamy Young ( Scandal, Prodigal Son ) as Martha Kent, Cristina Milizia ( DC Super Hero Girls ) as Maya, Petey & Kaylie, Eugene Byrd ( Bones, LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures ) as Ron Troupe, April Stewart ( South Park ) as Mrs. Ross, and Piotr Michael ( The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle ) as Perry White, as well as Cissy Jones ( Firewatch ) and David Chen ( Gotham ). Superman: Man of Tomorrow introduces a new producing vision to the DC Universe Movies series, which now numbers 41 films over its 13 years of existence. Supervising Producer Butch Lukic has a rich pedigree in DC animated productions, serving as producer on Constantine: City of Demons , Justice League Action and the Batman Unlimited franchise, as well as directing episodes of Justice League , Batman Beyond and Beware the Batman . Lukic brings a new visual aesthetic to Superman: Man of Tomorrow that departs from the animation styles – of previous producers Bruce Timm (23 films) and James Tucker (17 films) – thus far represented in the DC Universe Movies . See also Marvel Studios Releases Special Look At Upcoming Movies Chris Palmer ( Voltron: Legendary Defender ) is the director of Superman: Man of Tomorrow , utilizing a script by Tim Sheridan ( The Death of Superman ). Producers are Jim Krieg ( Batman: Gotham by Gaslight ) and Kimberly S. Moreau ( Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles ). Executive Producer is Sam Register. “ Superman: Man of Tomorrow is an inspiring retelling of the DC Universe Movies ’ backstory for The Man of Steel, taking the audience to his early days as an intern at the Daily Planet – and his beginnings as a learning-on-the-job DC Super Hero,” said Mary Ellen Thomas, Warner Bros. Home Entertainment Senior Vice President, Originals, Animation and Family Marketing. “Darren Criss and Zachary Quinto have wholeheartedly embraced their roles as Superman and Lex Luthor for this film, and the end result is a special addition to canon of films that every Superman fan will want to add to their collection.” Superman: Man of Tomorrow Special Features 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Combo Pack, Blu-ray Combo Pack and Digital Lobo: Natural Force of Chaos (New Featurette) – He’s the rude, crude, galactic bounty hunter who has been more than a thorn in the side of DC’s greatest heroes. This is a full throttle look at Lobo. Martian Manhunter: Lost and Found (New Featurette) – This is the personal journey of J’onn J’onzz. A stranger in a strange land who emerges from the shadows as a force for peace and justice. Look Back: Justice League vs. The Fatal Five (Featurette) – The Earth’s future hangs in the balance when the Justice League faces a powerful new threat – the Fatal Five. Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman seek answers as the time-traveling trio of Mano, Persuader and Tharok terrorize Metropolis in search of budding Green Lantern, Jessica Cruz – whom they need to be able to free remaining Fatal Five members Emerald Empress and Validus in order to carry out their sinister plan. But the Justice League discover an ally from another time in the peculiar Star Boy – brimming with volatile power, could he be the key to thwarting the Fatal Five? An epic battle against ultimate evil awaits! Look Back: Superman/Batman: Public Enemies (Featurette) – Based on the popular Jeph Loeb/Ed McGuinness comic series/graphic novel, the film finds United States President Lex Luthor using the oncoming trajectory of a Kryptonite asteroid to frame Superman and declare a $1 billion bounty on the heads of the Man of Steel and his “partner in crime,” Batman. Heroes and villains alike launch a relentless pursuit of Superman and Batman, who must unite – and recruit help – to stave off the action-packed onslaught, stop the asteroid, and uncover Luthor’s devious plot to take command of far more than North America. Talk Kristen Stewart kept her recent run of vintage sneaker moments going in West Hollywood on Sunday, stepping out in a pair of rare green-and-white Adidas Rekord sneakers at Film Independent Presents: An Intimate Evening and Reception with Kristen Stewart for “The Chronology of Water.” The event, held at The London West Hollywood at Beverly Hills, marked one of the final Los Angeles appearances tied to her upcoming directorial debut. The retro sneakers featured a smooth green leather upper with white serrated three-stripe detailing, a rounded toe and a flat rubber sole — a clean, low-profile build typical of Adidas’ early training shoes . Stewart styled the pair with black straight-leg jeans cuffed at the ankle, a white T-shirt and a rust-red zip jacket, keeping the look firmly in the vintage wheel. You May Also Like Related Stories EXCLUSIVE: Willy Chavarria and Adidas Turning '80s Basketball Sneaker Into a Plush Boot Undefeated Has Second Gucci-inspired Nike Air Max 95 Releasing Soon Kristen Stewart at The London West Hollywood at Beverly Hills on Sunday. Getty Images for Film Independent Originally introduced in 1959, the Rekord was designed as a lightweight trainer bridging Adidas ’ running and indoor-football categories. It’s one of the brand’s earliest thin-soled models, preceding later icons like the SL 72. The Rekord resurfaced in 2020 as the Adidas Overdub, a renamed update that preserved the original’s slim silhouette, serrated stripes and low rubber sole. A closer look at Kristen Stewart’s green and white vintage Adidas Rekord sneakers. Stewart’s choice follows her late October appearance at another “Chronology of Water” screening, where she wore red Converse trainers — continuing a visible preference for archival sneakers over heels. The mix of heritage footwear has become a throughline for the actor-director, who’s often alternated between vintage sportswear and Chanel tailoring on her press tour. Adidas has likewise been mining its past this year, most notably with the Italia ’60 Made in Italy reissue and renewed attention on slim-soled classics like the Samba and Taekwondo. “The Chronology of Water,” Stewart’s directorial debut, is adapted from Lidia Yuknavitch’s memoir and centers on a woman who finds her voice after a turbulent childhood marked by violence and addiction. The film premiered at Cannes back in May and is set for limited release in December. The Chronology of Water, adapted from Yuknavitch’s autobiographical bestseller, follows Lidia’s journey to find her own voice in an exploration of how trauma can be transformed into art through re-possessing our own bloody histories, particularly those uniquely experienced by bodies of women and girls. The Chronology of Water is directed by acclaimed Americana actress / producer / filmmaker Kristen Stewart , making her feature directorial debut after a few other short films. Stepping out in a look that balanced romance, her signature rock'n'roll defiance and a splash of sauciness, Kristen sported a sheer white lace dress teamed with killer black accessories. The Twilight alumni is currently on a press tour for her directorial debut, The Chronology of Water , which stars British actress Imogen Poots . A bohemian masterpiece complete with dramatic cuffs, a plunging neckline and ruffled collar. Kristen teamed her look with black stilettos and a silver pendant, and her tried-and-tested grunge inspired hair and makeup (we're obsessed with this bitty fringe.) © Getty Images Kristen Stewart, the director of The Chronology of Water But we also want to talk about Kristen's choice of pants (sorry Kristen.) Visible underwear goes hand-in-hand with sheer dresses, much like peaches and cream. And stars from Emily Ratajkowski to Kim Kardashian have all been seen sporting black underwear beneath mesh - and we are all for it this party season. But Kristen's choice of undies signal the unexpected return of a Y2K trend that hasn't yet popped up even as the early 00s have surged back into popularity. We're calling it - low-rise knickers are back. © Getty Images Kristen Stewart and Imogen Poots Naturally, with the waistband of choice of for the decade being scandalously low, the undergarments needed to follow suit. Unless you were feeling particularly raucous in which case you hoiked up the sides of your thong so they were visible. We are talking from experience. Nice work Kristen. We're off to buy new pants. And now, having collaborated with some of cinema\'s most celebrated filmmakers — from Kelly Reichardt ( Certain Women ) and Olivier Assayas ( Clouds Of Sils Marina ) to Pablo Larraín ( Spencer ) and David Cronenberg ( Crimes Of The Future ) — KStew is about to make her own directorial debut with The Chronology Of Water . Adapted from Lidia Yuknavitch\'s memoir, Stewart\'s film stars Imogen Poots as Yuknavitch, following the once promising young swimmer as she wrestles with various traumas and addictions on the path to finding her new calling as a writer. Check out the freshly released first trailer for the film below; Eight years in the making, it looks like The Chronology Of Water will prove to have been worth the wait for its director. Combining an intimate 16mm aesthetic with a fragmented narrative approach, Stewart\'s feature bow — if this first trailer is anything to go by — seems like an artistically bold, emotionally vulnerable opening gambit for the actor-turned-filmmaker, well placed to execute on the "unflinching portrait of survival, sexuality, and self-invention" promised by both its marketing material and its source text. And for Poots, last seen starring opposite Brett Goldstein in Apple TV\'s lo-fi romance All Of You , The Chronology Of Water represents a real chance to flex her considerable dramatic chops, too. The official synopsis for the movie reads as follows: "The film traces Lidia’s life from her earliest memories in the Pacific Northwest, as a promising swimmer, through fractured relationships, near-motherhood, addiction, and encounters with artistic heroes. Told as a fluid memory wash, the story transforms trauma into art, embodying Yuknavitch’s defiant voice that made her work a modern cult classic. It is not only a chronicle of a woman becoming a writer, but a visceral journey through the wreckage and resilience of a life lived against the grain." Among the ensemble featuring here alongside Poots are Thora Birch, Jim Belushi, Tom Sturridge, and Earl Cave. And we can look forward to seeing whether Kristen Stewart makes waves with The Chronology Of Water when her directorial debut washes into cinemas in the UK and Ireland on 6 February, 2026.
